title: Duplicate charges
text:
Duplicate charges
Section: Refunds and disputes > Card problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Seeing the same payment twice? Before disputing it, check whether one of them is just a hold.

## One says "Pending", the other "Completed"

This is usually a hold plus the final charge. Hotels, petrol stations and car rental companies often place a hold first and then charge the final amount separately. The hold drops off on its own within 7 calendar days. See Merchant holds and pre-authorizations.

## Both say "Completed"

You may really have been charged twice. Contact the merchant first and ask them to refund one of the payments. If they don't, open a dispute from either payment: **Report a problem** > **I was charged twice**.

## The amounts are slightly different

This often happens with payments in a foreign currency, or tips added after the payment. It's usually two different charges, not a duplicate.

If you paid twice yourself, for example because the first payment seemed to fail and you tried again, it's not a duplicate charge for dispute purposes. Ask the merchant for a refund of the extra payment.

title: Subscription charges I don't recognize
headings: I didn't sign up for this
text:
Subscription charges I don't recognize
Section: Refunds and disputes > Card problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

An unexpected monthly charge is often a subscription you signed up for, perhaps a free trial that turned into a paid plan.

## Find out what it is

Tap the payment in **Activity**. We show the merchant's name and, where available, their website or logo. The name on your statement can look different from the brand, for example the name of the parent company.

## Cancel the subscription

Cancel directly with the merchant, in their app or website, or through the App Store or Google Play if you subscribed there. Cancelling with the merchant is the only way to stop future charges for good.

## Block a merchant

You can also stop a merchant from charging your card again: **Cards** > **Recurring payments** > choose the merchant > **Block**. This doesn't cancel your subscription, and the merchant may still say you owe them.

## I didn't sign up for this

If you're sure you never subscribed, freeze your card and see Transactions I didn't make.

text:

The merchant says they've refunded you, but you don't see the money yet.

## It's been longer than the time above

Ask the merchant for the refund reference, sometimes called an ARN. Then contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us** and share it, and we'll trace the refund with the card network.

title: Partial refunds
headings: How do partial refunds show up?
I got less back than I expected
Can I get several partial refunds for one payment?
The merchant refunded too little and won't fix it
text:
Partial refunds
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sometimes a merchant refunds only part of a payment, for example when you return one item from an order.

## How do partial refunds show up?

As a separate refund line in **Activity**, for the amount the merchant refunded. The original payment stays as it was.

## I got less back than I expected

Check with the merchant first. Common reasons:

- They kept a delivery or restocking fee.
- Only some of the items were returned.
- The payment was in a foreign currency and the exchange rate has changed since you paid.

## Can I get several partial refunds for one payment?

Yes. A merchant can send more than one refund for the same payment, up to the original amount. Each one arrives separately.

## The merchant refunded too little and won't fix it

You can dispute the difference if you can show the merchant agreed to a full refund, or that what they kept goes against their own refund policy.

title: Refunds for QR payments
headings: How do I get a refund?
text:
Refunds for QR payments
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

QR payments go straight from your balance to the shop, through the QR payment network we're part of, so refunds work a little differently from card payments.

## How do I get a refund?

Ask the shop. They can refund you from their payment terminal or app, and the money comes back to your balance instantly, as soon as they send it.

## I paid the wrong amount

Show the shop your payment confirmation in **Activity**. They can refund the difference, or the whole payment so you can pay again.

## The shop won't refund me

Open the payment in **Activity** and tap **Report a problem**. Because QR payments don't go through the card network, there's no chargeback. We contact the shop directly and review the case ourselves, within the normal dispute deadlines for your country; see Dispute deadlines.

If you scanned a fake QR code stuck over the shop's real one, the payment went to someone else, not the shop. Report it as fraud straight away; see Reporting fraud.

title: Refunds to an expired or replaced card
headings: My card was replaced after I paid
What if the merchant says the refund failed?
text:
Refunds to an expired or replaced card
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Good news: you don't need your old card for a refund to reach you.

## My card was replaced after I paid

Refunds follow your account, not the card. If the merchant refunds the old card number, the refund still lands in your balance.

## My card has expired

The same applies. Expired and renewed cards are linked to the same account, so the refund arrives as normal.

## I closed my card

Refunds to a closed card still arrive in your balance, as long as your Sahla Pay account is open.

## What if the merchant says the refund failed?

Some merchants check the card before refunding and stop if it's expired. Ask them to try again anyway, or to refund you another way, such as store credit or a bank transfer.

If you've closed your whole Sahla Pay account, not just the card, it works differently: the refund is forwarded to your nominated bank account. See Refunds after account closure.

title: My dispute was rejected
text:
My dispute was rejected
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If we decided against your dispute, the email we sent explains why. Here's what you can do next.

## Common reasons

- The merchant showed the goods were delivered or the service was provided.
- The dispute was opened after the deadline.
- The payment was approved by you, for example with a one-time password.
- You didn't contact the merchant first.

## Can I appeal?

Yes, if you have new information. Reply from the case in **Help** > **My cases** within 15 calendar days of the decision and add the new evidence. A different person on our team will review it.

## What counts as new information?

Things we didn't have the first time, such as a tracking page showing the parcel was returned, or the merchant's written promise of a refund.

## Still not happy?

You can make a formal complaint; see Making a complaint.

Each dispute can be appealed only once. A second appeal with the same evidence is closed without a new review.

title: Evidence to include in a dispute
text:
Evidence to include in a dispute
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Good evidence makes a dispute faster and more likely to succeed. You can add files when you open the dispute, or later from the case in **Help** > **My cases**.

## What to include

| Problem | Useful evidence |
|---|---|
| Item not received | Order confirmation, expected delivery date, your messages with the merchant |
| Item not as described | Photos of what arrived, the listing or description you ordered from |
| Cancelled but charged | The cancellation confirmation, the merchant's cancellation policy |
| Charged twice | Both payments in **Activity**; a receipt showing one purchase |
| Refund promised, never came | The merchant's message promising the refund |

## Tips

- Screenshots are fine, but make sure the date and the merchant's name are visible.
- Add a short explanation in your own words. Arabic or English are both fine.
- Upload PDFs or photos, up to five files per upload.

## What not to send

Never send your full card number, CVV, PIN or password, even to us.

- Screenshots are fine, but make sure the date and the merchant's name are visible.
- Add a short explanation in your own words. Arabic or English are both fine.
- Upload PDFs or photos, up to five files per upload.

## What not to send

Never send your full card number, CVV, PIN or password, even to us.

title: Refunds after account closure
headings: Can I still open a dispute?
text:
Refunds after account closure
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If a refund arrives after you've closed your Sahla Pay account, you still get it. We forward it to the bank account you chose when you closed the account.

## How long does it take?

From when the refund reaches us:

| Country | Forwarded to your bank within |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 5 business days |
| UAE | 7 business days |
| Egypt | 10 business days |

You'll get an email when we send it.

## My bank account has changed

Contact us with the details of your new bank account in your own name. We'll ask you to confirm your identity first, because you can no longer log in to the app.

## Can I still open a dispute?

No. Disputes need an open account, which is why you can't close your account while a dispute is in progress.

If the bank account you nominated is closed and the forwarded refund is returned to us, we hold it for you. Contact us to claim it; we keep it until it's claimed or until we're legally required to pass it on as unclaimed money.

title: ATM didn't dispense cash
text:
ATM didn't dispense cash
Section: Refunds and disputes > Card problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The ATM took the money from your balance but gave you no cash, or less than you asked for.

## First, wait a little

Most failed ATM withdrawals are reversed automatically, often within the same day. Check **Activity** again later.

## Report it

If the money hasn't come back by the next day, open the withdrawal in **Activity** > **Report a problem** > **ATM didn't give me cash**. Tell us which ATM, the time, and how much cash you got, if any.

## How long does it take?

We check the ATM's records with the bank that owns it. Cases are resolved within:

- Saudi Arabia: 5 business days
- UAE: 7 business days
- Egypt: 10 business days

If the bank's records show the ATM had extra cash at the end of the day, the money is returned to your balance.

ATM withdrawal fees are refunded together with the amount. If the problem was at an ATM abroad, though, the case goes through the card network and can take up to 90 calendar days.

title: Transactions I didn't make
headings: Will I get my money back?
text:
Transactions I didn't make
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you see a payment or transfer you didn't make or approve, act straight away.

## Do this now

To protect your account:

1. Freeze your card: **Cards** > **Freeze**.
2. Change your password: **Profile** > **Security** > **Change password**.
3. Report the transaction: tap it in **Activity** > **Report a problem** > **I didn't make this**.

## Will I get my money back?

If you report an unauthorized transaction within 2 calendar days of noticing it, and you didn't share your password, PIN or one-time passwords with anyone, we refund it in full once we've confirmed it was unauthorized.

If you report it later, the most you'll lose is SAR 500 in Saudi Arabia, AED 500 in the UAE or EGP 2,000 in Egypt, unless you acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.

title: Transactions I didn't make
text:
Transactions I didn't make
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fraud > What counts as gross negligence?
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## What counts as gross negligence?

Sharing a one-time password with a caller, writing your PIN on your card, or letting someone else use your phone and app. If a transaction was approved with your OTP, we'll ask how the code was shared.

Payments you approved yourself because someone tricked you, for example a fake seller, aren't "unauthorized" under these rules, even though it's fraud. Report them through Reporting fraud, and we'll try to recover the money, but the protection above doesn't apply.

title: Refunds in a different currency
headings: Why didn't I get back exactly what I paid?
Can you refund me the difference?
The merchant refunded in my own currency
text:
Refunds in a different currency
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you paid in a foreign currency, the merchant refunds you in that same currency, and we convert it back.

## Why didn't I get back exactly what I paid?

Because the refund is converted on the day it arrives, not the day you paid. If the exchange rate moved in between, you may get a little more or a little less.

The markup in our rate also applies again when the refund is converted: 2.5% in Saudi Arabia, 2% in the UAE and 3% in Egypt. So even if the rate didn't move at all, a foreign-currency refund comes back slightly lower than the original payment.

## Can you refund me the difference?

No. Exchange rate differences on refunds aren't something we can refund, because we don't control the rate or when the merchant sends the refund.

## The merchant refunded in my own currency

Then no conversion is needed, and you get exactly the amount they sent.

title: Merchant refund policies vs Sahla Pay policies
text:
Merchant refund policies vs Sahla Pay policies
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Two different sets of rules can apply when you want your money back, and it helps to know which one you're dealing with.

## The merchant's policy

Each shop decides whether it accepts returns, for how long, and whether it refunds money, gives store credit, or exchanges items. This is between you and the merchant. Sahla Pay can't make a merchant accept a return that their policy doesn't allow.

## Sahla Pay's policies

Our rules cover:

- how quickly a refund reaches your balance once the merchant sends it (Refund timelines)
- disputes, when a merchant didn't deliver, charged you wrongly, or broke their own policy (Disputing a card transaction)
- payments you didn't make (Transactions I didn't make)

## An example

You bought shoes, changed your mind, and the shop's policy says "no refunds on sale items". That's the merchant's decision, and a dispute won't change it. But if the shop promised a refund in writing and never sent it, that's something we can help with.

title: Tracking a dispute
text:
Tracking a dispute
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can follow every dispute you've opened in the app.

## Check your case

To see where your dispute is:

1. Go to **Help** > **My cases**.
2. Tap the case. You'll see its status, the timeline so far, and any messages from our team.

## What the statuses mean

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Submitted | We've received it and it's waiting for review. |
| Need info | We've asked you something. Reply from the case. |
| Investigating | We're looking into it, or waiting for the other side. |
| Chargeback raised | We've sent it to the merchant's bank. |
| Resolved | A decision has been made. The outcome is in the case. |
| Closed | Finished. You can no longer add to it. |

## Adding information later

While a case is open, tap **Add information** to send more details or files. Adding information doesn't restart the investigation time.

title: Cancelling a dispute
headings: What happens to a temporary credit?
text:
Cancelling a dispute
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If the merchant refunded you, or you recognize the payment after all, you can cancel your dispute.

## Cancel a dispute

To cancel:

1. Go to **Help** > **My cases** and open the case.
2. Tap **Cancel dispute**.
3. Tell us why, for example "Merchant refunded me".

The case is closed straight away.

## What happens to a temporary credit?

If we gave you a temporary credit for the dispute, it's taken back from your balance when you cancel. If the merchant has refunded you as well, you'd otherwise get the money twice.

## Can I reopen it?

No. Once cancelled, a dispute can't be reopened, and you can't open a new one for the same payment.

Disputes that have already been sent to the merchant's bank as a chargeback can't be cancelled from the app. Message us from the case instead, and we'll withdraw it if the card network rules allow.

title: Disputes for international transfers
headings: Sent to the wrong person, or want it back
text:
Disputes for international transfers
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

International transfers go through other banks, sometimes several, so getting money back after it's sent is harder than for local transfers.

## Wrong details

If the IBAN or name was wrong, the receiving bank usually returns the transfer on its own. The amount comes back to your balance in your currency, at the exchange rate on the day it returns.

## Sent to the wrong person, or want it back

We can ask the receiving bank to return the money. This is called a recall. Open the transfer in **Activity** and tap **Report a problem** > **Recall this transfer**.

A recall costs SAR 50 in Saudi Arabia and AED 50 in the UAE. The receiving bank decides whether to return the money, and it usually needs the recipient's agreement. Recalls can take several weeks.

## Scams

If you were tricked into sending the transfer, report it as fraud straight away. The sooner we contact the receiving bank, the better the chance of stopping the money.

The recall fee is charged even if the receiving bank refuses to return the money, and it isn't refunded. If the bank does return it, intermediary banks may deduct their own fees, so you may get back less than you sent.

title: Bill paid to the wrong account
headings: The payment hasn't been posted yet
The account number belongs to someone else
text:
Bill paid to the wrong account
Section: Refunds and disputes > Payments
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Typed the wrong subscriber number, or picked the wrong company? Here's what you can do.

## The payment hasn't been posted yet

Bills are posted to the company within 1 business day in Saudi Arabia, 2 business days in the UAE and 1 business day in Egypt. Before that, the payment shows **Processing** in **Activity**. Contact us straight away through **Help** > **Chat with us**, and we'll try to stop it. We can't promise this, because many billers accept payments instantly.

## The payment has been posted

Only the company you paid can move or refund the money. Contact them with the payment receipt from **Activity** and ask them to:

- move the payment to your correct account, or
- refund it to you.

## The account number belongs to someone else

The company usually needs that customer's permission to refund, or will move the credit if you can show the payment was a mistake. We can give you an official confirmation of the payment to help.

Mobile recharges to a wrong number can't be reversed; see Mobile recharge.

text:

Section: Refunds and disputes

The quick version of everything about refunds.

## Who issues refunds for card payments?

The merchant. Ask them first. We can only step in with a dispute if they won't help.

## How long until a refund shows up?

After the merchant sends it: up to 7 business days in Saudi Arabia, 10 business days in the UAE and 14 business days in Egypt.

## Do refunds go back to my card or my balance?

Your balance. Your card spends from your balance, so it's the same thing.

Ask the shop. QR refunds arrive instantly once the shop sends them.

## A payment failed but I was charged

That's not a refund; it's reversed automatically within 2 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 5 business days in Egypt.

## Do you charge for refunds?

No. See Are there fees for refunds?.

## How long do I have to dispute a payment?

60 calendar days in Saudi Arabia, 45 calendar days in the UAE and 30 calendar days in Egypt, counted from the transaction date.

title: Fraudulent merchants
headings: I paid a fake shop by card
text:
Fraudulent merchants
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some online shops exist only to take payments and never deliver. If you think you've paid one, here's how we handle it.

## Signs of a fake shop

- Prices far below everywhere else, especially for phones, perfume and electronics.
- Only social media pages, no proper website or contact details.
- Asks you to pay by transfer to a personal account instead of by card.
- The shop disappears or blocks you after you pay.

## I paid a fake shop by card

Open a dispute from the payment as **Goods not received**. Card payments are protected by the card network rules, so you have a good chance of getting your money back. See Goods or services not received.

## I paid by transfer

Transfers to a person, rather than card payments, aren't covered by chargeback rules. Report it as fraud as soon as possible; we'll try to freeze the money in the recipient's account. See Reporting fraud.

## What happens to the merchant?

When we see several reports about the same merchant, we block card payments to them for all our customers and report them to the card network.

title: Goods or services not received
text:
Goods or services not received
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You paid by card but your order never arrived, or the service never happened.

## Before you dispute

- Check the tracking link and your spam folder for delivery updates.
- Contact the merchant and ask them to deliver or refund. Keep their reply.
- Wait until the expected delivery date has passed.

## Open the dispute

To dispute it:

1. Tap the payment in **Activity** > **Report a problem** > **I didn't receive it**.
2. Add the expected delivery date and your messages with the merchant.
3. Tap **Submit**.

## Deadlines

The usual dispute deadline is 60 calendar days from the transaction in Saudi Arabia, 45 calendar days in the UAE and 30 calendar days in Egypt. See Dispute deadlines.

For goods that are delivered late, for example a pre-order or furniture with a long delivery time, the deadline is counted from the expected delivery date instead of the payment date. But you need to wait at least 15 calendar days after that date before opening the dispute, to give the merchant a chance to deliver.

title: Are there fees for refunds?
text:
Are there fees for refunds?
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Getting a refund or opening a dispute is free. There are a few situations where fees you've already paid aren't returned.

## Refunds from merchants

Free. You get back whatever the merchant refunds. For refunds in a foreign currency, the exchange rate on the refund day applies; see Refunds in a different currency.

## Disputes and chargebacks

Free, whatever the outcome.

## Failed or returned transfers

If a transfer fails or is returned by the recipient's bank, the transfer fee is refunded too.

## Fees that aren't refunded

- Card top-up fees, if you later move the money out again.
- ATM fees abroad charged by the ATM's owner.

Recalling an international transfer has its own fee: SAR 50 in Saudi Arabia and AED 50 in the UAE. It's charged when you ask for the recall, and isn't refunded even if the recall fails. See Disputes for international transfers.

title: Ordering a physical card
text:
Ordering a physical card
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Every verified account gets a virtual card for online payments. If you also want a plastic card for shops and ATMs, you can order one in the app.

## Before you start

- Your account must be verified.
- Your delivery address must be in the same country your account is registered in.
- You need enough balance to cover the card fee.

| Country | Physical card fee |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | SAR 30 |
| UAE | AED 30 |
| Egypt | EGP 150 |

The fee is charged once, when you order. VAT is included.

## Order your card

To order a card:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap **Get a physical card**.
2. Check your name as it will be printed. It comes from your ID and can't be edited here.
3. Confirm or change your delivery address.
4. Tap **Order card** and confirm the fee.

## What happens next

We'll print and send your card, and you can track it under **Cards** > **Track delivery**. Delivery times for each country are in Card delivery times. When it arrives, activate it in the app before using it; see Activating your card.

title: Card delivery times
headings: Do I need to be home?
Can I use my card before it arrives?
text:
Card delivery times
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

After you order a physical card, we print it and send it by courier to the address you chose.

## How long does delivery take?

| Country | Delivery within |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 5 business days |
| UAE | 3 business days |
| Egypt | 10 business days |

The time starts the day after you order. Replacement cards take the same time.

## Can I track my card?

Yes. Go to **Cards** > **Track delivery**. Once the courier has it, you'll also get an SMS from them with a tracking link, and they'll call before delivering.

## Do I need to be home?

Someone has to sign for the card, and it can only be handed to you in person, with your ID. The courier tries twice. After two failed attempts, the card goes back to us and you'll need to arrange a new delivery in the app.

## Can I use my card before it arrives?

title: Activating your card
headings: Why does the shop's machine ask me to insert my card?
What happens to my old card?
text:
Activating your card
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your physical card arrives inactive, for your protection. Activate it in the app before you use it.

## Activate your card

To activate:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap **Activate card**.
2. Scan the QR code on the card's letter, or enter the last four digits of the card number.
3. Set your PIN. See Setting or changing your PIN.

Your card works for online and contactless payments straight away.

## Why does the shop's machine ask me to insert my card?

The first payment with a new card has to be a chip-and-PIN payment, not contactless. Insert the card and enter your PIN once, and contactless works after that.

## What happens to my old card?

If this card replaces an old one, the old card stops working as soon as you activate the new one. Cut it through the chip before throwing it away.

Cards that aren't activated within 90 calendar days of being sent are cancelled automatically, and you'd need to order a new one.

title: Setting or changing your PIN
headings: My card is blocked after wrong PIN attempts
text:
Setting or changing your PIN
Section: Cards > PIN
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You set your card PIN in the app. It's never sent by post or SMS.

## Set or change your PIN

To change your PIN:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap your card.
2. Tap **Card settings** > **Change PIN**.
3. Confirm it's you with your fingerprint, face or passcode.
4. Enter a new four-digit PIN twice.

The new PIN works straight away, everywhere.

## Choosing a PIN

Avoid your birth year, repeated digits like 1111, or simple sequences like 1234. The app won't accept the most common ones.

## I've forgotten my PIN

You can see it in the app: **Card settings** > **Show PIN**. Or simply set a new one.

## My card is blocked after wrong PIN attempts

See Card blocked after wrong PIN attempts.

title: Card blocked after wrong PIN attempts
headings: I unblocked it, but the ATM still says the PIN is blocked
text:
Card blocked after wrong PIN attempts
Section: Cards > PIN
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you enter the wrong PIN 3 times in a row, your card's PIN is blocked. This protects you if someone else has your card.

## What still works

Online payments and payments through Apple Pay or Google Pay keep working, because they don't use your PIN. Contactless payments below the no-PIN limit may also work.

## Unblock your PIN

To unblock it:

1. Go to **Cards** > **Card settings** > **Unblock PIN**.
2. Confirm it's you.
3. Check your PIN with **Show PIN**, or set a new one.

That's all. You don't need a new card.

## I unblocked it, but the ATM still says the PIN is blocked

Some ATMs remember the blocked status until you make a chip-and-PIN purchase. Make one small chip-and-PIN payment in a shop with your correct PIN, then try the ATM again.

If the ATM kept your card after the wrong PIN attempts, the card can't be returned to you. Freeze it in the app and order a replacement; the lost-card fee doesn't apply when an ATM keeps your card.

title: Freezing and unfreezing your card
headings: What still happens while my card is frozen?
text:
Freezing and unfreezing your card
Section: Cards > Security
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Can't find your card? Freeze it. Freezing stops new payments straight away, and you can undo it any time.

## Freeze your card

Go to **Cards** and tap **Freeze**. The card turns grey in the app. No new card payments, ATM withdrawals or online payments will go through.

## Unfreeze it

Found your card? Tap **Unfreeze**. It works again within seconds.

## What still happens while my card is frozen?

- Your balance is safe, and you can still send money and pay with QR codes.
- Refunds still arrive.
- Payments that were already approved before you froze the card can still complete.

## Freeze or report lost?

Freeze if you think the card is just misplaced. If you know it's lost or stolen, report it instead, and we'll cancel it and send a new one. See Reporting a lost or stolen card.

Recurring payments and subscriptions are also declined while the card is frozen. If you keep it frozen for a long time, update the card details with those merchants, or you may miss a payment.

title: Reporting a lost or stolen card
headings: Were there payments I didn't make?
text:
Reporting a lost or stolen card
Section: Cards > Security
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your card is lost or stolen, report it so we can cancel it and send you a new one.

## Report your card

To report it:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap your card.
2. Tap **Card settings** > **Report lost or stolen**.
3. Choose **Lost** or **Stolen**.
4. Confirm your delivery address for the replacement.

The old card is cancelled permanently, straight away. It can't be reactivated, even if you find it.

## Fees

A replacement for a lost or stolen card costs SAR 25 in Saudi Arabia, AED 25 in the UAE and EGP 100 in Egypt. See Card replacement fees.

## Were there payments I didn't make?

Check **Activity**. If you see anything you don't recognize, report it from the payment. See Transactions I didn't make.

## I don't have my phone

If your phone was stolen too, call the number for your country from another phone and we'll cancel the card for you. See My phone was stolen.

title: Replacing a damaged card
text:
Replacing a damaged card
Section: Cards > Replacement
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your card is cracked, bent, or the chip or contactless has stopped working, you can order a replacement. Your card number changes, but your balance and transaction history don't.

If your card is lost or stolen instead, freeze it straight away and follow Reporting a lost or stolen card.

## Order a replacement

To replace a damaged card:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap your card.
2. Tap **Card settings** > **Replace card** > **It's damaged**.
3. Confirm your delivery address.
4. Confirm the fee, if there is one.

Your old card keeps working until you activate the new one, so you can still use the parts that work, for example contactless if only the chip is broken.

## Fees

A replacement costs SAR 25 in Saudi Arabia, AED 25 in the UAE and EGP 100 in Egypt. The full fee table is in Card replacement fees.

Online subscriptions and saved cards (for example in shopping apps) won't update automatically. Add the new card details once it arrives.

If the card stops working within 12 months of when it was issued, and it hasn't been physically broken (for example, the chip just stopped reading), the replacement is free. Choose **It stopped working** instead of **It's damaged** in step 2, and the fee is removed before you confirm.

title: Virtual cards
headings: Can I have more than one?
Can I delete a virtual card?
text:
Virtual cards
Section: Cards > Virtual cards
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A virtual card is a card that lives in the app. It has its own number, expiry date and CVV, and spends from your balance like a physical card.

## How do I get one?

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, every verified account gets a virtual card automatically. You'll find it under **Cards**. In Egypt, tap **Cards** > **Get a virtual card**, because the card has a one-time fee and we don't create it until you ask.

## Is it free?

| Country | Virtual card |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | free |
| UAE | free |
| Egypt | EGP 25, one-time |

## Can I have more than one?

Yes, up to 3 virtual cards. Some people keep one just for subscriptions, so they can freeze it without affecting their other payments. In Egypt, the one-time fee applies to each extra card.

## Where can I use it?

Online, in apps, and in shops through Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay, where available in your country. You can't use it at ATMs or for chip-and-PIN payments, because there's no physical chip.

## Can I delete a virtual card?

Yes: **Card settings** > **Close card**. Subscriptions on that card will stop working.

title: Adding your card to Apple Pay
text:
Adding your card to Apple Pay
Section: Cards > Mobile wallets
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Pay with your iPhone or Apple Watch in shops, apps and online.

| Country | Apple Pay |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | available |
| UAE | available |
| Egypt | not available yet |

## Add your card

To add your card:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap your physical or virtual card.
2. Tap **Add to Apple Wallet**.
3. Follow the steps on screen and accept the terms.

You can also add it from the Wallet app, but adding it from Sahla Pay is faster because your details are filled in for you.

## Paying with Apple Pay

Hold your iPhone near the card reader and confirm with Face ID or Touch ID. Apple Pay payments aren't limited by the contactless no-PIN limit, because you confirm them on your phone.

If you freeze your card in Sahla Pay, Apple Pay stops working too. Replacing your card, though, doesn't update Apple Pay automatically: remove the old card from Wallet and add the new one.

Section: Cards > Mobile wallets

Android users can pay with their phone using Google Pay or, on Samsung phones, Samsung Pay.

title: Contactless payments and limits
headings: Why did the reader ask for my PIN for a small payment?
text:
Contactless payments and limits
Section: Cards > Paying in shops
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Tap your card on the card reader to pay. For small amounts, you don't need a PIN.

## What's the no-PIN limit?

| Country | Contactless without PIN, per payment |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | SAR 300 |
| UAE | AED 500 |
| Egypt | EGP 600 |

Above this amount, the reader asks for your PIN.

## Why did the reader ask for my PIN for a small payment?

For security, after several contactless payments in a row the card asks for your PIN once, even below the limit. It then works without PIN again.

## Can I turn contactless off?

Yes: **Cards** > **Card settings** > **Contactless payments**.

## Is phone payment the same?

Payments with Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay don't have this limit, because you confirm them with your phone's lock. See Adding your card to Apple Pay.

The first payment with a new or replacement card must be chip and PIN. Contactless only works after that.

title: Card declined
text:
Card declined
Section: Cards > Problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your card was declined, the app usually tells you why. Tap the declined payment in **Activity**.

## "Insufficient balance"

Your balance didn't cover the payment. For payments in another currency, the amount after conversion counts, so a payment can be declined even when it looks like you have enough.

## "Card frozen"

Unfreeze it in **Cards**.

## "Daily spending limit reached"

Card payments are limited to SAR 20,000 a day in Saudi Arabia, AED 20,000 in the UAE and EGP 50,000 in Egypt, or less if you lowered it yourself. See Card spending controls.

## "Blocked by your settings"

You've turned off online, contactless, ATM or international payments. Turn the setting back on in **Card settings**.

## "Incorrect PIN" or "PIN blocked"

See Card blocked after wrong PIN attempts.

## "Declined for security"

Our systems stopped the payment because it looked unusual. Check your notifications to confirm it was you, then try again.

## No reason shown

The merchant's bank may have declined it, often for online payments abroad. Try again later, or use your virtual card or a mobile wallet.

title: Using your card abroad
headings: Do I need to tell you I'm travelling?
text:
Using your card abroad
Section: Cards > Using your card abroad
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your Sahla Pay card works in shops, online and at ATMs worldwide, wherever the card network logo is shown.

## Do I need to tell you I'm travelling?

No. But check that **International payments** is turned on in **Cards** > **Card settings**. It's on by default.

## What does it cost?

- Card payments: no fee, but the exchange rate includes our markup of 2.5% (Saudi Arabia), 2% (UAE) or 3% (Egypt).
- ATM withdrawals abroad: SAR 15, AED 10 or EGP 50 per withdrawal, plus the markup. The ATM's owner may charge as well.

See Currency conversion and exchange rates.

## Tips

- Always choose to pay in the local currency.
- Keep the app installed and your phone number active, because we may send you a code to approve a payment.
- Know how to freeze your card in the app, in case it's lost.

Some countries are blocked for card payments because of sanctions or high fraud. Payments there are always declined. See Restricted countries and transactions.

Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Withdraw cash from your Sahla Pay balance at any ATM that shows the card network logo.

## How much can I withdraw?

Up to SAR 5,000 a day in Saudi Arabia, AED 5,000 in the UAE and EGP 15,000 in Egypt. The ATM may have its own lower limit per withdrawal.

## How much does it cost?

In your own country: SAR 3 in Saudi Arabia, AED 2 in the UAE and EGP 10 in Egypt per withdrawal. Full details are in ATM withdrawal fees.

In Saudi Arabia, your first 2 withdrawals each calendar month are free.

## Can I check my balance at the ATM?

Use the app instead. Balance checks at ATMs are free, but some ATMs show the wrong amount for prepaid accounts.

## Can I use my virtual card?

No. ATMs need the physical card.

## The ATM didn't give me cash

See ATM didn't dispense cash.

The free withdrawals in Saudi Arabia only apply at ATMs in Saudi Arabia. A withdrawal abroad is always charged, and it doesn't use up one of your free withdrawals.

title: Online payments and 3-D Secure
headings: I got an approval request for a payment I'm not making
Some payments don't ask me to approve
text:
Online payments and 3-D Secure
Section: Cards > Paying online
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

When you pay online, many shops ask you to approve the payment in the Sahla Pay app. This is 3-D Secure, and it stops anyone using your card details without your phone.

## How does it work?

1. You enter your card details on the shop's website.
2. We send a notification to your phone.
3. Open it, check the shop name and amount, and tap **Approve**.

You have 5 minutes to approve. After that, the payment is cancelled and you'll need to start again.

## I didn't get the notification

Open the Sahla Pay app directly. Pending approvals appear at the top of the home screen. If notifications are off, you'll get an SMS code instead.

## I got an approval request for a payment I'm not making

Tap **Decline**, freeze your card, and report it. Someone has your card details.

## Some payments don't ask me to approve

That's normal. Some merchants, such as subscriptions you've already approved once, don't use 3-D Secure for repeat payments.

Payments approved with 3-D Secure are treated as authorized by you. If you approve a payment that turns out to be a scam, the protection for unauthorized transactions doesn't apply.

title: Card expiry and renewal
headings: Will I get a new card automatically?
Do I need to activate it?
text:
Card expiry and renewal
Section: Cards > Replacement
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Physical cards are valid for 4 years. The expiry date is printed on the card and shown under **Cards** > **Show details**.

## Will I get a new card automatically?

Yes. We send your new card about 30 calendar days before your current one expires, to the address in your profile. Renewal cards are free.

## Do I need to activate it?

Yes, in the app, like any new card. Your old card keeps working until it expires or until you activate the new one, whichever comes first.

## Will my card number change?

The number stays the same, but the expiry date and CVV change. Update your card details with online shops and subscriptions after you activate the new card.

## Virtual cards

Virtual cards are renewed in the app automatically. The new expiry date and CVV appear on the card when the old one expires.

If your account is dormant, or your ID has expired, we don't send a renewal card. Make your account active or update your ID first, and then order a renewal from **Cards**. See Dormant account fees.

title: My card hasn't arrived
headings: It's been longer than the delivery time
Is there a fee for the new card?
text:
My card hasn't arrived
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Cards are delivered within 5 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 10 business days in Egypt. If yours hasn't arrived yet, check these first.

## Check the tracking

Go to **Cards** > **Track delivery**. The status shows whether the courier has your card, tried to deliver it, or returned it to us.

## The courier couldn't deliver

After two failed attempts, the card is returned to us. You'll see **Returned** in the tracking. Tap **Arrange delivery** to choose a new date or a different address.

## It's been longer than the delivery time

Wait 5 business days after the expected delivery date, in case of delays. If it still hasn't come, tap **Card not received** in the tracking screen. We'll cancel that card and send a new one.

## Is there a fee for the new card?

No. A card that never arrived is replaced free of charge.

If the tracking shows the card was delivered and signed for, but you didn't receive it, it's treated as possibly stolen. The card is cancelled, and the replacement fee of SAR 25 in Saudi Arabia, AED 25 in the UAE or EGP 100 in Egypt applies, unless the courier confirms a delivery mistake. See Card replacement fees.

title: Changing your card delivery address
text:
Changing your card delivery address
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can change where your card is delivered until the courier has picked it up.

## Change the address

To change it:

1. Go to **Cards** > **Track delivery**.
2. Tap **Change address**.
3. Enter the new address, or choose your work address.
4. Tap **Save**.

## The courier already has it

Once the status shows **With courier**, the address can't be changed in the app. Use the link in the courier's SMS to reschedule the delivery, or wait for it to be returned to us and then arrange a new delivery.

## Can I collect it myself?

No. Cards are only delivered, not collected from an office.

The delivery address has to be in the country your account is registered in. If you're abroad, we can't send your card there; it waits for you until you're back. Cards that aren't activated within 90 calendar days of being sent are cancelled, so arrange the delivery and activate it before then.

title: Card spending controls
headings: Do controls apply to my virtual card?
text:
Card spending controls
Section: Cards > Security
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Decide where and how your card can be used. Changes apply straight away.

## Your controls

Go to **Cards** > **Card settings** to turn these on or off:

- **Online payments**
- **Contactless payments**
- **ATM withdrawals**
- **International payments**, meaning payments in shops or ATMs outside your country and online payments in a foreign currency

## Daily spending limit

The default daily card spending limit is SAR 20,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 20,000 in the UAE and EGP 50,000 in Egypt. You can lower it under **Card settings** > **Daily limit**, but you can't raise it above the default.

ATM withdrawals have their own daily limit; see ATM withdrawals.

## Block a merchant

To stop a merchant from charging your card again, go to **Cards** > **Recurring payments**, choose the merchant and tap **Block**.

## Do controls apply to my virtual card?

Each card has its own settings. Changing your physical card's controls doesn't change your virtual card.

title: Merchant holds and pre-authorizations
headings: What does a hold look like?
Can you release a hold early?
text:
Merchant holds and pre-authorizations
Section: Cards > Paying in shops
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some merchants reserve money on your card before charging you the final amount. This is called a hold or pre-authorization.

## Where do holds happen?

Hotels, car rental, petrol stations, and some online shops and subscriptions that check your card with a small amount.

## What does a hold look like?

A **Pending** payment in **Activity**. The amount is taken from your available balance but hasn't been paid to the merchant.

## When is it released?

When the merchant charges the final amount, the hold is replaced by the real payment. If the merchant doesn't charge anything, the hold drops off on its own within 7 calendar days.

## Can you release a hold early?

We can't, because the merchant decides. Ask the merchant to cancel the pre-authorization; once they do, the money is usually back within a day.

Hotels and car rental companies are allowed to keep a hold for longer, up to 30 calendar days, for example to cover damage or extra nights. These holds are released when the merchant closes your booking, not after the standard time.

title: Can I get a second card?
headings: Can I have two physical cards?
Can I get a card for my husband, wife or child?
Why have more than one virtual card?
Is there a fee for extra virtual cards?
text:
Can I get a second card?
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can have one physical card and up to 3 virtual cards on your account.

## Can I have two physical cards?

No. Each account has one physical card at a time. If you order a replacement, the old one stops working.

## Can I get a card for my husband, wife or child?

Not on your account. Cards can only be used by the account holder. Your family member can open their own Sahla Pay account and get their own card. You can then send them money instantly and for free.

## Why have more than one virtual card?

Some people use one for subscriptions and one for one-off online shopping, so they can freeze or close one without affecting the other.

## Is there a fee for extra virtual cards?

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, no. In Egypt, each virtual card has a one-time fee of EGP 25.

title: Closing your card
headings: What happens to payments on that card?
Can I get a new card later?
text:
Closing your card
Section: Cards > Closing a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can close a card without closing your Sahla Pay account. Your balance stays, and you can keep sending money and paying with QR codes.

## Close a card

To close it:

1. Go to **Cards** and tap the card.
2. Tap **Card settings** > **Close card**.
3. Confirm.

Closing a card is permanent. If you only want to stop it for a while, freeze it instead; see Freezing and unfreezing your card.

## What happens to payments on that card?

Subscriptions and recurring payments on the card will be declined. Refunds to the card still reach your balance.

## Can I get a new card later?

Yes. Order a new physical card from **Cards**. The normal card fee applies.

Closing your physical card doesn't refund the fee you paid for it, even if you closed it soon after ordering.

title: Recurring card payments
headings: What happens if my balance is too low?
text:
Recurring card payments
Section: Cards > Paying online
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Subscriptions, memberships and other regular payments can be charged to your Sahla Pay card automatically.

## Where can I see them?

Go to **Cards** > **Recurring payments**. We list every merchant that has charged your card on a repeating basis, with the last payment date and amount.

## How do I stop one?

Cancel with the merchant. That's the only way to end the agreement. To stop the merchant from charging your card anyway, tap the merchant and choose **Block**. See Subscription charges I don't recognize.

## What happens if my balance is too low?

The payment is declined. Many merchants try again a few days later, and may pause your subscription in the meantime.

## My card was replaced

Many merchants receive your new card details automatically through the card network and keep charging without interruption. Others don't. Check **Recurring payments** after a replacement.

Because some merchants update automatically, a subscription can keep charging your new card even after you replaced the card to get away from it. Blocking the merchant is the reliable way to stop it.

title: Card PIN not received
headings: I activated my card but didn't set a PIN
Someone called and gave me my PIN
The letter with my card mentions a PIN
text:
Card PIN not received
Section: Cards > PIN
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We don't send PINs by post, SMS or email. You choose your PIN yourself in the app when you activate your card.

## I activated my card but didn't set a PIN

Setting a PIN is the last step of activation. If you closed the app before finishing it, a temporary PIN was created for you. Go to **Cards** > **Card settings** > **Show PIN** to see it, and change it whenever you like.

## Someone called and gave me my PIN

That's a scam. We never call with your PIN and we never ask for it. Hang up, change your PIN in the app and report the call through **Help** > **Report fraud**.

## The letter with my card mentions a PIN

The letter only explains how to activate your card. If it contains a PIN or a sealed PIN slip, it didn't come from us; don't use the card, and contact us.

For how to change your PIN, see Setting or changing your PIN.

title: Name and design on your card
headings: Whose name is printed on the card?
Can I have my name in Arabic?
Can I choose a card design?
text:
Name and design on your card
Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Whose name is printed on the card?

Yours, in English capital letters, taken from your verified ID. You can't choose a nickname or another person's name.

## My name is too long

Card names can be up to 21 characters. If yours is longer, we shorten it automatically, usually by using initials for middle names. You can see the printed version before you order.

## Can I have my name in Arabic?

Not on the card itself. Card networks only support Latin letters. Your Arabic name is used everywhere in the app if your app language is Arabic.

## Can I choose a card design?

There's one design for physical cards. Virtual cards come in several colours, which you can change in **Card settings** > **Card colour**.

If the name on your ID is spelled differently in English from what you'd expect, the card follows your ID. Correct your ID details first if they're wrong; see Changing the name on your account.

title: Wallet balance limits
headings: What happens if I reach it?
text:
Wallet balance limits
Section: Fees and limits > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

There's a maximum amount you can keep in your Sahla Pay balance. It depends on whether you're verified and where your account is registered.

| | Saudi Arabia | UAE | Egypt |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unverified account | SAR 5,000 | AED 3,000 | EGP 20,000 |
| Verified account | SAR 100,000 | AED 75,000 | EGP 300,000 |

The limit includes everything in your account, including Pockets.

## What happens if I reach it?

Top-ups and incoming transfers that would take you over the limit are declined in full and returned to the sender. Card payments and outgoing transfers still work.

## Can I raise it?

Verifying your account raises it to the verified level. Above that, the balance limit can't be increased, even with a temporary limit increase; that only affects how much you can send per day. See Can I increase my limits?.

Refunds are the one exception: a refund is credited even if it takes your balance over the limit. You won't be able to add more money until you're back under it.

title: ATM withdrawal limits
text:
ATM withdrawal limits
Section: Fees and limits > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

How much cash you can withdraw with your Sahla Pay card each day.

| Country | Daily ATM limit |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | SAR 5,000 |
| UAE | AED 5,000 |
| Egypt | EGP 15,000 |

The limit applies to all withdrawals in a day combined, in your country and abroad. Withdrawals abroad are counted in your own currency, after conversion.

ATMs often have their own limit per withdrawal, which can be lower than ours. If you need more, make several withdrawals; each one is charged separately.

The daily ATM limit is separate from your card spending limit and your transfer limits. Using one doesn't reduce the others. Daily limits reset at midnight in your account's country.

title: Dormant account fees
text:
Dormant account fees
Section: Fees and limits > Account fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

An account becomes dormant when you haven't made any transaction yourself for a while. Money you receive, interest and fees don't count; it has to be something you did, like a payment, a transfer or a top-up.

| Country | Dormant after | Monthly dormancy fee |
|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 12 months | no fee |
| UAE | 12 months | AED 10 per month |
| Egypt | 18 months | EGP 20 per month |

We'll email you and send an app notification before your account becomes dormant, so you have time to use it.

To make your account active again, log in and make any transaction, even a small top-up. The fee stops from the next month.

The dormancy fee is only taken from money in your balance. It never takes your balance below zero, and if your balance is zero, nothing is charged and nothing is owed. Accounts that stay dormant with a zero balance may eventually be closed; see Dormant accounts.

title: Why was I charged a fee?
text:
Why was I charged a fee?
Section: Fees and limits > Fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Every fee appears in **Activity** as its own line or on the transaction it belongs to. Tap it to see what it's for.

## "Dormancy fee"

Your account had no activity from you for a long time. See Dormant account fees.

## "Card top-up fee"

You added money with a debit card. Bank transfer top-ups are free. See Top-up fees.

## "ATM fee"

You withdrew cash. In Saudi Arabia, the first few withdrawals each month are free. See ATM withdrawal fees.

## "Transfer fee"

You sent money to a bank account or abroad. Transfers to other Sahla Pay users are free.

## "VAT"

Value added tax on one of our fees. See VAT on fees.

## A fee I don't recognize

Some charges aren't ours: a fee taken by an ATM's owner, a merchant's convenience charge, or a difference caused by a currency conversion. If you still think a fee is wrong, contact us from the transaction with **Report a problem**.

title: How daily and monthly limits reset
headings: Does a cancelled transfer give me my limit back?
text:
How daily and monthly limits reset
Section: Fees and limits > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## When do daily limits reset?

At midnight in the country your account is registered in: Riyadh time for Saudi Arabia, UAE time for the UAE, and Cairo time for Egypt. It doesn't matter where you are when you make the payment.

## When do monthly limits reset?

At midnight at the start of the 1st day of each calendar month. It's a calendar month, not a rolling month counted from your first payment.

## Which limits reset this way?

All of them: transfer limits, card spending, ATM withdrawals, QR payments and, for unverified accounts, the monthly receiving limit. Balance limits don't reset, because they're about how much you hold, not how much you move.

## Does a cancelled transfer give me my limit back?

Yes, as soon as it's cancelled or fails.

A refund doesn't. If you pay for something and get a refund later, the original payment still counts towards that day's and month's limit.

title: VAT on fees
headings: Which fees include VAT, and which have it added?
Can I get a tax invoice?
text:
VAT on fees
Section: Fees and limits > Fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Our fees are subject to value added tax (VAT) at the rate of the country your account is registered in.

| Country | VAT rate |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 15% |
| UAE | 5% |
| Egypt | 14% |

## Which fees include VAT, and which have it added?

Card fees (physical card and replacement) already include VAT; the amount you see is what you pay. Most other fees, such as transfer, top-up and ATM fees, have VAT added on top. The fee schedule for your country shows which is which.

## What isn't taxed?

The money you send, receive or spend is not taxed by us. The exchange rate markup has no VAT either.

## Can I get a tax invoice?

Yes. Go to **Profile** > **Statements** > **Tax invoice** and choose the month.

Free services have no VAT. When a fee is waived, for example a free ATM withdrawal in Saudi Arabia or a free card replacement, there's no VAT to pay either.

title: Fee changes and notice period

text:
Fee changes and notice period
Section: Fees and limits > Fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We sometimes change our fees and limits. When we do, we tell you in advance.

## How much notice do you give?

At least 30 calendar days before a fee goes up or a new fee is introduced. We tell you by email and in the app, and the updated fee schedule is published on the date the change is announced.

## What if I don't agree?

You can close your account for free before the change takes effect. See Closing your account.

## Do you give notice when fees go down?

Not always. Fee reductions and new free services can apply immediately.

## Where can I find the current fees?

In the fee schedule for your country: Saudi Arabia, UAE or Egypt.

The notice period doesn't apply to changes required by law or a regulator, such as a change in the VAT rate. These apply from the date the law sets, which can be sooner.

Payments with Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay aren't limited this way, because you confirm them on your phone.

title: Limits on receiving money
headings: Is there a limit on how much I can receive?
What happens if a payment would go over the limit?
Will you ask about large amounts?
text:
Limits on receiving money
Section: Fees and limits > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Is there a limit on how much I can receive?

For verified accounts, there's no separate receiving limit. The only limit is your maximum balance: SAR 100,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 75,000 in the UAE and EGP 300,000 in Egypt.

For unverified accounts, you can receive up to SAR 10,000 per calendar month in Saudi Arabia, AED 7,500 in the UAE and EGP 40,000 in Egypt, as well as the lower balance limit.

## What happens if a payment would go over the limit?

It's declined and returned to the sender in full. We don't accept part of it.

## Will you ask about large amounts?

Possibly. If you receive more than SAR 50,000 in a month in Saudi Arabia, AED 50,000 in the UAE or EGP 250,000 in Egypt, we may ask where the money comes from. See Source of funds questions.

Refunds aren't counted towards the monthly receiving limit for unverified accounts, and they're credited even if you've reached it.

title: Requesting a temporary limit increase
headings: How much and for how long?
text:
Requesting a temporary limit increase
Section: Fees and limits > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Need to make a large one-off payment, like a deposit for a flat or a car? Verified accounts in Saudi Arabia and the UAE can ask for a higher daily transfer limit for a short time.

## How much and for how long?

| Country | Temporary daily limit | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | up to SAR 50,000 | 7 calendar days |
| UAE | up to AED 40,000 | 7 calendar days |
| Egypt | not available | |

## Before you start

- Your account must be verified, and your ID must be valid.
- Have a document showing what the payment is for, such as a tenancy contract, car sale agreement or invoice.

## Request an increase

To request it:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Limits** > **Request a temporary increase**.
2. Enter the amount and what it's for.
3. Upload your document.
4. Tap **Submit**.

We review requests within 1 business day. If approved, the new limit starts straight away.

## Things to know

You can ask for a temporary increase up to 2 times per calendar year. Your monthly limit doesn't change during the increase, and the balance limit stays the same too. See Can I increase my limits?.

title: Keeping your account secure
text:
Keeping your account secure
Section: Security
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We protect your account with encryption, fraud monitoring and checks on every new device. A few habits on your side make it much safer still.

## The basics

- Use a password of at least 8 characters that you don't use anywhere else.
- Turn on fingerprint or face login, so you don't type your password in public.
- Keep your phone's own screen lock on.
- Install app updates when they come out. They often include security fixes.

## Never share

Your password, PIN, one-time passwords and card CVV are for you only. Sahla Pay staff will never ask for them, by phone, chat, SMS, email or social media. See We will never ask for your OTP.

## Watch out for

- Calls or messages saying your account is blocked and asking you to "verify" it
- Links in SMS messages that open a login page
- Sellers who want you to pay by transfer instead of by card

## Built-in protection

The app locks itself after 5 minutes without use. Logins on new devices need a code and a selfie. See Trusted devices.

If anything seems wrong, freeze your card in the app and contact us. See Reporting fraud.

title: One-time passwords (OTP)
headings: How long is a code valid?
Will Sahla Pay ever ask me for my code?
Can I get codes by email instead?
text:
One-time passwords (OTP)
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A one-time password (OTP) is a 6-digit code we send by SMS to your registered phone number. We ask for it when you log in on a new device, add a recipient, send money abroad, or change your security settings.

## How long is a code valid?

Each code works once and expires after 5 minutes. If it expires, request a new one. Only the latest code works, so older codes stop working as soon as you ask for a new one.

## I didn't get the code

Wait 60 seconds and tap **Resend code**. If it still doesn't arrive, see Not receiving OTP codes.

## Will Sahla Pay ever ask me for my code?

No. Nobody from Sahla Pay will ever call, message or email you asking for an OTP, your PIN or your password. If someone asks, it's a scam, even if the caller knows your name or recent transactions. Hang up and report it from **Help** > **Report fraud**.

## Can I get codes by email instead?

Not at the moment. Codes are only sent by SMS to the phone number on your account. If you've changed your number, update it first; see Changing your registered phone number.

title: Not receiving OTP codes
text:
Not receiving OTP codes
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

One-time passwords are sent by SMS to your registered phone number. If they're not arriving, try these steps in order.

## Quick checks

1. Make sure your phone has signal. Turn airplane mode on and off.
2. Check that the number in the app is the one in your phone. You'll see the last digits on the code screen.
3. Look in your SMS spam or blocked messages folder.
4. If your phone storage is full, delete some messages.

## Resending the code

Wait 60 seconds, then tap **Resend code**. You can resend up to 3 times. After that, you'll need to wait 30 minutes before trying again.

## Abroad?

Codes are sent to your number while you're roaming, but some networks abroad delay or block them. Turn on roaming, or connect to Wi-Fi and use the in-app approval if you're already logged in.

## Changed your number?

You need to update it first; see Changing your registered phone number.

If you suddenly stop receiving codes and your phone shows no signal at all, your SIM may have been swapped by someone else. Call your mobile operator immediately, and see SIM swap protection.

title: Account locked after failed login attempts
headings: My card is still working, is that normal?
text:
Account locked after failed login attempts
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## "Too many attempts. Try again later."

To protect your money, the app locks login after 5 wrong passwords in a row. The lock lasts 30 minutes. After that you can try again.

## I've forgotten my password

Don't keep guessing. Tap **Forgot password** on the login screen, confirm your phone number with the code we send, and set a new password. Resetting your password ends the lock straight away.

## My card is still working, is that normal?

Yes. A login lock only affects the app. Your card and any scheduled transfers keep working. If you think someone else has been trying to get into your account, freeze your card from the website or by calling the number on the back of your card.

## Locked again?

If your account is locked 3 times within one day, it's restricted for your protection, and the timer no longer unlocks it. Resetting your password won't lift it either. Only our support team can, after checking your identity. Contact us through **Help** on the login screen.

title: Recognizing phishing and scam messages
text:
Recognizing phishing and scam messages
Section: Security > Scams
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Scammers often pretend to be Sahla Pay, a bank, a delivery company or a government office. Their goal is to get your login details or one-time passwords, or to make you send money.

## Common tricks

- **"Your account will be suspended."** A message with a link to "verify" your account. The link opens a fake login page.
- **"Your parcel is waiting."** A delivery fee request with a payment link.
- **A call from "the fraud team".** The caller knows your name and asks you to read out a code "to cancel a suspicious payment". The code actually approves a payment.
- **Prize or refund messages.** You've "won" something or are owed a refund, and need to enter your card details.

## How to tell it's fake

- We never send links that ask you to log in.
- We never ask for your OTP, PIN, password or CVV.
- Official messages from us appear in the app's **Inbox** as well.

## What to do

Don't click, don't reply, don't call back on numbers in the message. Report it through **Help** > **Report fraud**. If you've already shared a code or details, freeze your card and change your password immediately; see Reporting fraud.

title: Reporting fraud
headings: Will I get my money back?
text:
Reporting fraud
Section: Security > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you've been scammed, or think someone has access to your account, report it straight away. The faster we know, the better the chance of stopping the money.

## Report fraud in the app

To report it:

1. Freeze your card: **Cards** > **Freeze**.
2. Go to **Help** > **Report fraud**.
3. Choose what happened and pick the transactions involved.
4. Tell us how it happened, in as much detail as you can.

## Call us

The fraud line is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in all three countries. The number is in **Help** > **Call us** and on the back of your card.

This is different from our general support hours in Egypt, which are 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM Cairo time, every day. Fraud calls in Egypt are always answered, even outside those hours.

## What happens next

We try to stop or freeze the money with the recipient's bank or Sahla Pay account, and we secure your account. You'll get a case number to follow up in **Help** > **My cases**.

## Will I get my money back?

It depends on what happened. If someone used your account without your permission, see Transactions I didn't make. If you were tricked into sending money yourself, we'll try to recover it, but we can't guarantee it.

We also recommend reporting scams to the police. We'll give you a statement of the transactions if they ask for one.

title: Someone else accessed my account
text:
Someone else accessed my account
Section: Security > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Signs include a login alert you don't recognize, a changed email or phone number, or transactions you didn't make.

## Secure your account now

To lock someone out:

1. Change your password: **Profile** > **Security** > **Change password**.
2. Check **Profile** > **Security** > **Trusted devices** and remove any device you don't recognize.
3. Freeze your card.
4. Check your email address and phone number under **Personal details**.

## If you can't log in

The other person may have changed your password or phone number. Call our fraud line, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. We'll lock the account and help you get back in after checking your identity.

## Check your transactions

Go through **Activity** and report anything you didn't make. See Transactions I didn't make.

## How did it happen?

Usually through a shared code, a fake login page, or someone who knows your password and had access to your phone. See Recognizing phishing and scam messages.

title: Changing your password
headings: What happens after I change it?
text:
Changing your password
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Change your password

To change it while logged in:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Security** > **Change password**.
2. Enter your current password.
3. Enter a new password, at least 8 characters long, twice.
4. Confirm with the code we send to your phone.

## Forgot your password?

On the login screen, tap **Forgot password**. Enter the code we send to your phone, take a quick selfie, and choose a new password.

## Password rules

Your password must include letters and numbers, and can't be the same as your last three passwords. Avoid your name, phone number or date of birth.

## What happens after I change it?

You stay logged in on the device you used. All other devices are logged out and will need the new password.

Changing your password also removes all your trusted devices except the one you're using. The next time you log in on another device, you'll need a code and a selfie again.

title: Biometric login
headings: Can someone else's fingerprint open my app?
text:
Biometric login
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Log in and approve payments with your fingerprint or face instead of typing your password.

## Turn it on

To turn on biometric login:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Security** > **Biometric login**.
2. Switch it on and enter your password once.
3. Confirm with your fingerprint or face.

## Which phones are supported?

Any phone with Face ID, Touch ID, or Android fingerprint or face unlock that's registered as "strong" biometrics in your phone's settings.

## It stopped working

If you add a new fingerprint or face to your phone, biometric login in Sahla Pay switches off automatically, for your safety. Log in with your password and turn it on again.

## Can someone else's fingerprint open my app?

Any fingerprint or face saved on your phone can unlock the app. Only keep your own biometrics on the phone you use for Sahla Pay.

Biometric login can't be used for everything. Changing your phone number, password or email always needs your password and a code, even if biometric login is on.

title: Trusted devices
headings: How does a device become trusted?
Where can I see my devices?
text:
Trusted devices
Section: Security > Devices
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A trusted device is a phone or tablet where you've logged in and confirmed it's you. You can have up to 3 trusted devices at a time.

## How does a device become trusted?

The first time you log in on a device, you enter your password, a code we send by SMS, and take a selfie. After that, the device is trusted and you just log in normally.

## Where can I see my devices?

**Profile** > **Security** > **Trusted devices**. You'll see each device's name, when it was added and when it was last used.

## Remove a device

Tap the device and choose **Remove**. It's logged out straight away. Do this if you sell or lose a phone.

## I've reached the maximum

Remove an old device before adding a new one. The app will ask you to choose one when you log in on a new device.

For your protection, for 24 hours after you add a new trusted device, you can't send money to new recipients or send money abroad from it. Payments to people you've paid before work normally. See Using Sahla Pay on a new phone.

title: SIM swap protection
headings: Signs your SIM has been swapped
text:
SIM swap protection
Section: Security > Devices
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

In a SIM swap scam, a criminal convinces your mobile operator to move your number to a new SIM card, so they receive your codes. We watch for this.

## What we do

When we detect that the SIM card for your number has changed, we pause all outgoing transfers, local and international, for 24 hours. You'll get an email explaining why.

## I changed my SIM myself

That's fine. If you got a new SIM, for example after losing your phone or switching to an eSIM, the pause ends on its own after 24 hours. To lift it sooner, take a selfie in **Profile** > **Security** > **Confirm it's me**.

## Signs your SIM has been swapped

- Your phone suddenly shows **No service** or **SOS only**, in a place where it normally works.
- You get a message from your operator about a SIM change you didn't ask for.
- You stop receiving calls and texts.

If this happens, contact your mobile operator first, then our fraud line. See Reporting fraud.

Card payments in shops keep working during the pause, because they don't depend on SMS codes. If you think your SIM was swapped by someone else, freeze your card as well.

title: We will never ask for your OTP
headings: Why is the OTP so important?
What do I do if someone asks?
text:
We will never ask for your OTP
Section: Security > Scams
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Nobody from Sahla Pay will ever ask you for:

- a one-time password (OTP) or verification code
- your PIN
- your password
- your card's CVV
- remote access to your phone, for example through a screen-sharing app

This applies to calls, WhatsApp, SMS, email, social media and in person. It applies even if the person says they're from our fraud team, even if they know your name, card number or recent payments, and even if the call seems to come from our real number. Caller numbers can be faked.

## Why is the OTP so important?

The code is what approves a payment, a new device or a new recipient. Anyone who has it can act as you. When you read a code to someone, you're approving whatever they're doing.

## What do I do if someone asks?

Hang up. Then open the Sahla Pay app yourself, or call the number on the back of your card. If you've already shared a code, freeze your card and call our fraud line straight away.

This applies to calls, WhatsApp, SMS, email, social media and in person. It applies even if the person says they're from our fraud team, even if they know your name, card number or recent payments, and even if the call seems to come from our real number. Caller numbers can be faked.

## Why is the OTP so important?

The code is what approves a payment, a new device or a new recipient. Anyone who has it can act as you. When you read a code to someone, you're approving whatever they're doing.

## What do I do if someone asks?

Hang up. Then open the Sahla Pay app yourself, or call the number on the back of your card. If you've already shared a code, freeze your card and call our fraud line straight away.

title: Suspicious login alerts
text:
Suspicious login alerts
Section: Security > Devices
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We send you an alert by SMS and email when someone tries to log in to your account from a new device.

## What does the alert say?

The device type, the approximate location, and the time. It also has a link to the app, never to a login page.

## It was me

You don't need to do anything. If you were trying to log in on a new phone, finish the steps on that phone.

## It wasn't me

Someone may know your password. Open the app on your usual phone and:

1. Tap **This wasn't me** in the alert in your **Inbox**. This blocks the new device.
2. Change your password.
3. Check **Trusted devices** for anything you don't recognize.

They can't log in without the SMS code and your selfie, so if you haven't shared a code, your account is still safe. See Someone else accessed my account if you think they got in.

## The location looks wrong

Locations are approximate and based on the internet connection. A mobile network can show a different city, especially when using mobile data.
