title: Investment scams and fake sellers
text:
Investment scams and fake sellers
Section: Security > Scams
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some scams don't steal your login. They convince you to send money yourself.

## Investment scams

You're promised large, quick returns on crypto, forex or a "trading platform". Often you see small profits at first, and then you're asked to pay "fees" or "taxes" to withdraw. The money is never returned.

Warning signs: guaranteed returns, pressure to act fast, contact through WhatsApp or social media, and requests to send money to a person rather than a regulated company.

## Fake sellers

Cars, phones, rental flats and pets are common. The seller wants a deposit by transfer, often because they're "abroad", and the item never exists.

Pay by card where you can. Card payments have dispute rights that transfers don't. See Fraudulent merchants.

## Romance and job scams

Someone you met online, or a recruiter, asks you to send money or to receive money and pass it on. Receiving and forwarding money for someone else can make you part of a crime.

If you've sent money to a scammer, report it immediately; see Reporting fraud. Because you approved the payment, it isn't covered by our protection for unauthorized transactions, but we'll try to stop the money if we can still reach it.

title: My phone was stolen
headings: Can the thief use my app?
How do I get back into my account?
Do I need a new card?
text:
My phone was stolen
Section: Security > Devices
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your money is protected by your phone's screen lock, your Sahla Pay password and biometric login. Still, act quickly.

## What should I do first?

1. Call your mobile operator and block your SIM.
2. Call our fraud line from another phone, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. We'll block the stolen device and freeze your card.
3. If you can, log in on another device and remove the stolen phone from **Trusted devices**.

## Can the thief use my app?

Not without unlocking your phone and then getting past the app's own lock. The app locks itself after 5 minutes without use, and payments need your fingerprint, face or passcode.

## How do I get back into my account?

On your new phone, install the app and log in with your password. You'll need a code sent to your number, so get a replacement SIM from your operator first. Then take a selfie to confirm it's you. See Using Sahla Pay on a new phone.

## Do I need a new card?

If your card was in a phone case or wallet that was also stolen, yes; see Reporting a lost or stolen card. Otherwise, keep your card frozen until your phone situation is sorted, then unfreeze it.

title: How we protect your card details
headings: When you use a mobile wallet
text:
How we protect your card details
Section: Security > Cards
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your card details are stored and processed according to the card industry's security standard (PCI DSS).

## In the app

Your full card number and CVV are hidden until you tap **Show details** and confirm with your fingerprint, face or passcode. They're never shown in notifications, emails or screenshots of your receipts.

## When you pay online

Most online payments need your approval in the app (3-D Secure), so card details alone aren't enough to pay.

## When you use a mobile wallet

Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay don't share your real card number with the shop. They use a separate device number that only works on your phone.

## Our staff

Support staff can see the last four digits of your card, never the full number, CVV or PIN.

## What you can do

Don't save your card details in browsers or apps you don't trust. Use a separate virtual card for online shopping and subscriptions, so you can close it without affecting your physical card.

title: Account restrictions due to suspicious activity
headings: What does a restriction look like?
Can you tell me exactly why?
text:
Account restrictions due to suspicious activity
Section: Security > Restrictions
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We may restrict an account when we see activity that could mean fraud, someone else using the account, or a breach of our terms.

## Why do restrictions happen?

- Payments that look like a scam, for example many transfers to new recipients in a short time
- Logins from unusual places or devices, together with other unusual activity
- Receiving money that other customers report as stolen
- Not answering a source of funds or re-verification request
- Repeated login lockouts

## What does a restriction look like?

A banner in the app explains what's restricted. Usually outgoing transfers and card payments are paused, while you can still log in, see your balance and receive money.

## What do I do?

Follow the steps in the banner. See Removing a restriction from your account.

## Can you tell me exactly why?

Usually, yes. In some cases, the law doesn't allow us to explain a restriction, for example when it relates to an investigation by the authorities. When that happens, we'll tell you we can't share the reason, and we may not be able to say how long it will last.

title: Removing a restriction from your account
headings: How long does the review take?
text:
Removing a restriction from your account
Section: Security > Restrictions
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your account is restricted, the banner in the app tells you what we need. Most restrictions are lifted once you've completed those steps.

## Lift a restriction

To get it removed:

1. Tap the banner on the home screen, or go to **Help** > **My cases**.
2. Complete what's asked. This could be a selfie, your ID, answers about recent transactions, or documents about the source of your money.
3. Tap **Submit**.

## How long does the review take?

Once we have everything, we review it within 2 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 5 business days in Egypt.

## Can I speed it up?

Sending complete, clear documents the first time is the fastest way. Calling us doesn't speed up the review.

## Restricted after login lockouts?

If your account was restricted after being locked several times, support has to unlock it after checking your identity. See Account locked after failed login attempts.

If we decide to close the account instead of lifting the restriction, we'll tell you, and your balance will be paid out to a bank account in your name. See When Sahla Pay closes an account.

title: Two-step verification
text:
Two-step verification
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Two-step verification means you need two things to get into your account or approve important actions: something you know (your password or passcode) and something you have (your phone).

## When is it used?

It's always on for:

- logging in on a new device
- adding a new recipient
- sending money abroad
- changing your phone number, email or password

You can't turn it off for these.

## Extra protection: approve every login

To be asked for a code every time you log in, even on your trusted phone, go to **Profile** > **Security** > **Code at every login** and switch it on.

## Passcode for payments

You can also require your app passcode, instead of fingerprint or face, for all transfers: **Profile** > **Security** > **Passcode for transfers**.

If you lose access to your phone number, two-step verification means you can't get codes until you've updated the number. Keep your phone number up to date, and see Changing your registered phone number.

title: Security FAQ
headings: Will Sahla Pay ever call me and ask for a code?
How long is a code valid?
What happens if I enter the wrong password too often?
How many devices can I use?
Is the fraud line open at night?
What if someone takes money from my account?
Why can't I send money after getting a new phone?
text:
Security FAQ
Section: Security
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Will Sahla Pay ever call me and ask for a code?

Never. Anyone asking for your OTP, PIN or password is a scammer.

## How long is a code valid?

5 minutes.

## What happens if I enter the wrong password too often?

After 5 wrong attempts, login is locked for 30 minutes.

## How many devices can I use?

Up to 3 trusted devices.

## Is the fraud line open at night?

Yes, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt.

## What if someone takes money from my account?

Report it straight away. If you report an unauthorized transaction within 2 calendar days and didn't share your details, we refund it in full.

## Why can't I send money after getting a new phone?

For 24 hours after adding a new device, sending to new recipients and abroad is paused. This protects you if someone else set up your account on their phone.

title: App won't open or keeps crashing
text:
App won't open or keeps crashing
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Try these steps in order. Most problems are fixed by the first two.

## 1. Update the app

Open the App Store or Google Play and install the latest version of Sahla Pay.

## 2. Restart your phone

Turn it off completely and on again. This clears temporary problems.

## 3. Check your phone's software

The app needs iOS 16 or later on iPhone, or Android 9 or later on Android. See Supported phones and operating systems.

## 4. Free up space

If your phone storage is almost full, the app may close unexpectedly. Delete some photos, videos or unused apps.

## 5. Reinstall

Delete the app and install it again. Your money and history are safe; they're stored with us, not on your phone. You'll need your password and a code to log in again.

## Still crashing?

Contact us through **Help** on the login screen, and tell us your phone model and what you were doing when it closed. If the app won't open at all, call the number on the back of your card. Your card keeps working in the meantime.

title: Supported phones and operating systems
headings: My phone is no longer supported
text:
Supported phones and operating systems
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Which phones can I use?

- iPhone with iOS 16 or later
- Android phones with Android 9 or later, with Google Play services

## Can I use a tablet?

Yes, iPads and Android tablets that meet the same requirements work. The app is designed for phones, so some screens look stretched.

## Huawei phones without Google Play

Phones without Google Play services can't install the app from an official store, and we don't support installing it from other sources.

## Is there a web version?

No. Sahla Pay is app-only. You can't log in from a computer.

## My phone is no longer supported

When we stop supporting an older version, we tell you in the app first. After the end date, the app won't open on that phone, but your account, balance and card keep working. Log in on a supported phone to manage your money.

Rooted or jailbroken phones are blocked, even if they meet the requirements above, because we can't keep your account secure on them.

title: Can't log in
headings: Nothing happens when I tap Log in
text:
Can't log in
Section: Help > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Find the message you see, or what's happening, below.

## "Incorrect password"

Check that caps lock is off and that you're using the right phone number. If you've forgotten it, tap **Forgot password**. Don't keep guessing: after 5 wrong attempts, login is locked for 30 minutes. See Account locked after failed login attempts.

## "We couldn't send a code"

See Not receiving OTP codes.

## "New device detected"

You're logging in on a phone we don't recognize. Enter the code and take a selfie when asked. See Trusted devices.

## "Your account is restricted"

Follow the steps on screen, or see Removing a restriction from your account.

## The selfie keeps failing

See Selfie check failed.

## Biometric login doesn't work

Log in with your password, then turn biometric login on again in **Profile** > **Security**. It turns off automatically when you add a new fingerprint or face to your phone.

## Nothing happens when I tap Log in

Check your internet connection, and update the app.

title: Notifications not arriving
headings: After a new phone or reinstall
text:
Notifications not arriving
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Notifications tell you about payments, transfers and security events, and they're how you approve online card payments.

## Check your phone settings

- **iPhone:** Settings > Notifications > Sahla Pay > Allow Notifications.
- **Android:** Settings > Apps > Sahla Pay > Notifications, and make sure battery saving isn't stopping the app.

## Check the app settings

In **Profile** > **Notifications**, make sure the types you want are switched on.

## Focus and do-not-disturb modes

These can hide notifications. Add Sahla Pay to your allowed apps.

## After a new phone or reinstall

Open the app once and log in. Notifications only start after the first login on a device.

Security alerts are also sent by SMS and email, so you'll still get those even if app notifications are off. Payment approvals for online shopping are different: if notifications are off, they arrive as an SMS code instead, which can be slower.

headings: My balance is lower than I expected
The balance is different on two devices
text:
Balance not updating
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your balance looks wrong, first pull down on the home screen to refresh it.

## Money I expected hasn't appeared

Check how it was sent:

- From another Sahla Pay user: instant. Ask them to check the transfer status.
- From a bank: depends on your country; see Topping up by bank transfer.
- From abroad: up to 3 business days; see Receiving money from abroad.
- A refund: see Refund timelines.

## My balance is lower than I expected

Look for **Pending** items in **Activity**. Card holds and pending transfers reduce your available balance before they're completed. See Merchant holds and pre-authorizations.

Money in Pockets isn't included in your main balance on the home screen. Tap **Pockets** to see it.

## The balance is different on two devices

Log out and back in on the device showing the old balance. If it's still different, contact us.

title: The app asks me to update
headings: Why do I have to update?
text:
The app asks me to update
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Why do I have to update?

Updates include security fixes and changes needed by our partners. When an older version is no longer safe to use, we make the update required.

## Can I skip it?

Optional updates can be skipped. Required updates can't: the app won't let you continue until you update.

## The update won't install

- Check you have enough free storage.
- Connect to Wi-Fi.
- Make sure your phone meets the requirements: iOS 16 or Android 9 or later.

## Will I lose anything?

No. Updating keeps you logged in and doesn't change your balance, cards or history.

If your phone can't install the required update because its operating system is too old, the app stops working on that phone. Your card and account keep working, but you'll need a supported phone to use the app again.

title: Error codes
text:
Error codes
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some error messages in the app include a code. Here's what the most common ones mean.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| E101 | No internet connection | Check Wi-Fi or mobile data and try again |
| E204 | Session expired | Log in again |
| E310 | Daily limit reached | Try again after midnight, or see Daily and monthly transfer limits |
| E315 | Recipient can't receive this amount | The recipient's balance limit would be exceeded |
| E402 | Insufficient balance | Top up and try again |
| E450 | Blocked for security | Check your notifications and confirm it was you |
| E512 | Recipient bank not responding | Try again later |
| E600 | Verification required | Verify your identity in **Profile** |
| E701 | Device not supported | See Supported phones and operating systems |
| E900 | Something went wrong on our side | Try again in a few minutes |

If you see a code that isn't listed, or the same error keeps coming back, contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us** and include the code.

| E310 | Daily limit reached | Try again after midnight, or see Daily and monthly transfer limits |
| E315 | Recipient can't receive this amount | The recipient's balance limit would be exceeded |
| E402 | Insufficient balance | Top up and try again |
| E450 | Blocked for security | Check your notifications and confirm it was you |
| E512 | Recipient bank not responding | Try again later |
| E600 | Verification required | Verify your identity in **Profile** |
| E701 | Device not supported | See Supported phones and operating systems |
| E900 | Something went wrong on our side | Try again in a few minutes |

If you see a code that isn't listed, or the same error keeps coming back, contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us** and include the code.

title: Using Sahla Pay on a new phone
text:
Using Sahla Pay on a new phone
Section: Help > Devices
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Moving to a new phone? Your account isn't stored on your phone, so nothing is lost.

## Set up the new phone

To start using Sahla Pay on it:

1. Install the app from the App Store or Google Play.
2. Log in with your phone number and password.
3. Enter the code we send by SMS. Your SIM must be in the new phone, or your number must be active on it as an eSIM.
4. Take a selfie to confirm it's you.
5. Turn on biometric login again.

## Remove the old phone

Go to **Profile** > **Security** > **Trusted devices** and remove your old phone, especially if you're selling it or giving it away.

## Cards in mobile wallets

Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay don't move with you. Add your card again on the new phone.

For 24 hours after setting up a new phone, sending money to new recipients and international transfers are paused. Payments to recipients you've used before, card payments and QR payments work as normal. See Trusted devices.

text:
Changing the app language
Section: Help > Settings
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The app is available in Arabic and English.

## Change the language

To switch:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Settings** > **Language**.
2. Choose **العربية** or **English**.

The app restarts in the new language. In Arabic, the layout switches to right-to-left.

## What changes?

All app screens, notifications and in-app messages. Emails and SMS messages follow the same language from the next message on.

- Merchant names in **Activity**, which appear as the merchant sends them
- Your name on your card, which is always in English letters
- Documents and statements you already downloaded

## Can I talk to support in Arabic?

Yes. Chat and phone support are available in Arabic and English, whatever your app language.

title: Statements and transaction history
headings: How far back can I see my transactions?
Can I use it as proof for a visa or rental?
text:
Statements and transaction history
Section: Help > Statements
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## How far back can I see my transactions?

The app shows your full history for the last 24 months, in **Activity**.

## Can I search my history?

Yes. Use the search bar in **Activity** to find a merchant, a person or an amount, or filter by date and type.

## What's in a statement?

Your opening and closing balance, every transaction with its date, amount and fee, and the account details banks or embassies usually ask for. Statements are available in Arabic and English.

## Can I use it as proof for a visa or rental?

Yes. Statements are stamped digitally and include a reference number that can be checked with us.

## I need older transactions

For anything older than 24 months, request a statement from **Help** > **Chat with us**. It's sent to your email within 5 business days.

Pending transactions aren't included in statements until they're completed. If a statement shows a different balance from the app, check **Activity** for pending items. To download a statement, see Downloading a statement.

Section: Help > Statements

PDFs open in any PDF reader. CSV files open in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets. If Arabic text looks broken in a CSV, open it with the UTF-8 option in your spreadsheet app.

Section: Help > App problems

## Check your connection

Most slowness comes from a weak connection. Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, or move closer to your router.

## Update and restart

Install the latest version of the app, then restart your phone.

## Clear space

If your phone storage is almost full, everything gets slower, including Sahla Pay.

## Is it everyone?

Sometimes the problem is on our side. We post service updates in the app's **Inbox** and on our social media accounts.

Still slow? See App won't open or keeps crashing for more steps.

title: Camera not working during verification
headings: The camera opens but won't focus
Can I upload a photo instead?
text:
Camera not working during verification
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The app needs your camera to scan your ID and take your selfie.

## Allow camera access

- **iPhone:** Settings > Sahla Pay > Camera, switch on.
- **Android:** Settings > Apps > Sahla Pay > Permissions > Camera > Allow.

Then close and reopen the app.

## Black screen

Another app may be using the camera. Close video calls and camera apps, and try again.

## The camera opens but won't focus

Clean the lens, and hold the ID a bit further away. Good light helps a lot.

## Can I upload a photo instead?

No. For security, IDs and selfies have to be captured live in the app. Photos from your gallery aren't accepted.

## Front camera not working

The selfie uses your front camera, and every verification method needs it, including Nafath and UAE Pass. If it's broken, contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us**. We can verify you on a video call instead, on another device of your own. Don't log in on someone else's phone to verify; it would become a trusted device on your account (see Trusted devices).

title: Payment stuck on processing
text:
Payment stuck on processing
Section: Help > Payments
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If a payment screen keeps spinning, or a payment shows **Processing** in **Activity**, don't try again straight away. You could end up paying twice.

## The screen froze while paying

Close the app and open it again. Check **Activity**:

- **Completed**: the payment went through. Don't pay again.
- **Failed**: nothing was taken. You can try again.
- **Processing**: wait. Most payments finish within a few minutes.

## Still processing after an hour

The other side hasn't confirmed yet, often a bank or a biller. If it ends up failing, the money comes back within 2 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 5 business days in Egypt. See A failed payment was deducted from my balance.

## Bill payments

Bills can show **Processing** until they're posted to the company. See Paying bills.

## Transfers

See Pending transfers.

title: Contacting customer support
text:
Contacting customer support
Section: Help > Contact us
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The fastest way to reach us is in the app: tap **Help** > **Chat with us**. You'll talk to a person, in Arabic or English, and your account details are already attached, so you don't need to repeat them.

## When are you available?

| Country | Chat and phone hours |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 24 hours a day, 7 days a week |
| UAE | 24 hours a day, 7 days a week |
| Egypt | 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM Cairo time, every day |

Outside these hours, you can still leave a chat message and we'll reply when we open.

## Can I call you?

Yes. The number for your country is on the back of your card and under **Help** > **Call us**. If you call, we'll confirm your identity with a code sent to your phone.

## Urgent: lost card or fraud

You don't need to wait for us. Freeze your card instantly in **Cards** > **Freeze**. It works at any time, including outside support hours, and you can unfreeze it yourself if you find the card.

## Email

We don't handle account questions by email, because we can't confirm who is writing. Emails asking for personal details that appear to come from us are not from us.

title: Accessibility features
text:
Accessibility features
Section: Help > Settings
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We want everyone to be able to use Sahla Pay on their own.

## Screen readers

The app works with VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack on Android, in Arabic and English. Buttons, amounts and card details are labelled for screen readers.

## Text size and contrast

The app follows your phone's text size setting. You can also turn on **High contrast** in **Profile** > **Settings** > **Accessibility**.

## Verification

If you can't complete the ID scan or selfie because of a disability, contact us. We can verify you on an assisted video call instead.

## Cards

Our physical cards have a notch on the short edge so you can tell which way to insert them.

## Support

Chat is available for customers who are deaf or hard of hearing. If you'd like someone you trust to help you with a call, we can talk to them while you're present, but you'll still need to confirm your identity yourself.

title: Using Sahla Pay with a VPN
headings: Can I use the app with a VPN?
I'm abroad and need a VPN to reach other services
text:
Using Sahla Pay with a VPN
Section: Help > App problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Can I use the app with a VPN?

You can, but it can cause problems. Our security systems look at where your connection comes from. A VPN can make it look like you're logging in from another country.

## What can go wrong?

- Extra security checks, like a new code or a selfie
- Transfers held for review
- Login blocked, if the VPN shows a location in a country we can't serve

## What should I do?

Turn the VPN off while you use Sahla Pay, especially when logging in on a new device or sending money.

## I'm abroad and need a VPN to reach other services

Turn it off just for Sahla Pay. Our app works from abroad without a VPN, wherever mobile data or Wi-Fi is available.

If the VPN makes your connection appear to come from a restricted country, transactions are blocked automatically, even if you're actually at home. See Restricted countries and transactions.

title: Location permission
headings: Why does the app ask for my location?
Do I have to allow it?
text:
Location permission
Section: Help > Settings
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Why does the app ask for my location?

To protect your account. Knowing roughly where you are helps us tell your real payments from fraud, for example when someone uses your card in another country while your phone is at home.

## Do I have to allow it?

No. The app works without it. Without your location, though, we may ask for extra checks more often, and some card payments abroad may be declined until you confirm them in the app.

## Do you track me?

No. We only check your location when you open the app or make a payment, not in the background. We don't share it with merchants or advertisers.

## How do I change it?

- **iPhone:** Settings > Sahla Pay > Location, and choose **While Using the App** or **Never**.
- **Android:** Settings > Apps > Sahla Pay > Permissions > Location.

The nearby-ATM map also uses your location; without it, you'll need to search by area.

title: Deleting the app vs closing your account
headings: If I delete the app, is my account closed?
What happens to an account I stop using?
How do I close my account properly?
text:
Deleting the app vs closing your account
Section: Help > Account
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## If I delete the app, is my account closed?

No. Deleting the app only removes it from your phone. Your account, balance and card stay active, and you can log in again by reinstalling it.

## What happens to an account I stop using?

It stays open. If you make no transactions for 12 months in Saudi Arabia, 12 months in the UAE or 18 months in Egypt, it becomes dormant, and a monthly dormancy fee may apply in the UAE and Egypt. See Dormant account fees.

## How do I close my account properly?

From the app: **Profile** > **Account settings** > **Close account**. Your balance is sent to your bank. See Closing your account.

## I already deleted the app

Reinstall it and log in to close your account, or to move your balance out first.

title: Terms of use summary
text:

Section: Legal > Terms

This is a plain-language summary of the main points in our terms of use. The full terms, which you accepted when you opened your account, are in **Profile** > **Legal** > **Terms of use**. If this summary and the full terms differ, the full terms apply.

## Your account

- Sahla Pay is a personal e-wallet, for individuals only. One account per person.
- Your account belongs to the country where you opened it, and that country's rules apply.
- Your balance isn't a bank deposit and doesn't earn interest.

## Your responsibilities

- Keep your password, PIN and codes secret, and tell us straight away if you think someone else knows them.
- Keep your details, ID and phone number up to date.
- Don't use your account for business, illegal activity or on behalf of someone else.

## Our responsibilities

- Carry out your payments correctly and on time.
- Protect your money and data.
- Refund unauthorized transactions according to Transactions I didn't make.

## Ending the agreement

You can close your account at any time, for free. We can close it too, in the situations described in When Sahla Pay closes an account.

## Changes

We can change the terms with 30 calendar days notice. See Changes to our terms.

title: Privacy notice summary
text:
Privacy notice summary
Section: Legal > Privacy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A short summary of how we handle your personal data. The full privacy notice is in **Profile** > **Legal** > **Privacy notice**.

## What we collect

- Identity details: name, date of birth, nationality, ID number and photo, and your selfie
- Contact details: phone number, email, address
- Financial details: your transactions, balance, linked bank accounts and cards
- Device details: phone model, app version, IP address and, if you allow it, location

## Why we use it

To verify your identity, run your account and payments, prevent fraud and money laundering, meet our legal obligations, and improve the app. We don't sell your data.

## Who we share it with

Only those who need it to provide our service or because the law requires it: banks and card networks that process your payments, identity verification partners, regulators and authorities, and our service providers under strict contracts.

## Your rights

You can ask for a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, and object to marketing. Some data we must keep by law, even if you ask us to delete it. See How long we keep your data.

## Marketing

You can turn off marketing messages in **Profile** > **Notifications**. Service and security messages can't be turned off.

title: Closing your account
text:
Closing your account
Section: Account > Closing your account
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can close your Sahla Pay account at any time, for free. Deleting the app does not close your account; see Deleting the app vs closing your account.

## Before you start

- Download any statements you need. After closing, you won't have access to the app. We keep records for 24 months in the app, and you'd have to ask support for older ones.
- Cancel subscriptions and saved card payments, and tell anyone who sends you money regularly.
- Make sure there are no pending transfers.

## Close your account

To close your account:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Account settings** > **Close account**.
2. Tell us why (optional, but it helps us).

title: Dormant accounts
headings: When does an account become dormant?
What changes when an account is dormant?
text:
Dormant accounts
Section: Legal > Account status
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

An account is dormant when you haven't made any transaction yourself for a set period. Money you receive and fees we charge don't count as activity.

## When does an account become dormant?

| Country | Dormant after no activity for |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 12 months |
| UAE | 12 months |
| Egypt | 18 months |

We'll remind you by email and in the app before it happens.

## What changes when an account is dormant?

- Your card stops working and isn't renewed.
- You can still log in, see your balance and receive money.
- In the UAE and Egypt, a monthly dormancy fee applies. See Dormant account fees.

## Reactivate your account

Log in and make any transaction yourself, such as a top-up or a payment. If your ID has expired in the meantime, you'll need to update it first.

## Closure of dormant accounts

If a dormant account has a zero balance for a further 12 months, we may close it, with notice by email. Accounts with money in them are never closed just for being dormant. Their balance stays yours, and we're required by law to keep it safe for you or pass it to the authority responsible for unclaimed funds.

title: When Sahla Pay closes an account
headings: Why might you close my account?
How much notice will I get?
text:
When Sahla Pay closes an account
Section: Legal > Account status
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

In some situations, we may close an account ourselves.

## Why might you close my account?

- The account was opened with false or someone else's details.
- The account is used for fraud, scams or other illegal activity.
- You've seriously or repeatedly broken our terms, for example by using a personal account for a business.
- You haven't completed required checks, such as source of funds or re-verification, after several reminders.
- The account has been dormant with a zero balance for a long time. See Dormant accounts.

## How much notice will I get?

Usually at least 60 calendar days, by email and in the app, so you have time to move your money.

## What happens to my money?

Your balance is paid to a bank account in your name, within 3 business days in Saudi Arabia, 5 business days in the UAE or 7 business days in Egypt after the account closes.

If we close an account because of fraud or a legal requirement, we may close it immediately, without notice, and we may not be able to tell you why. In these cases, the balance may be held until the authorities allow us to release it.

title: Making a complaint
text:
Making a complaint
Section: Legal > Complaints
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you're unhappy with our service, tell us. Complaints are handled by a separate team from day-to-day support.

## Make a complaint

To raise a complaint:

1. Go to **Help** > **Make a complaint**.
2. Explain what happened and what you'd like us to do.
3. Attach any screenshots or documents that help.
4. Tap **Submit**.

You can also make a complaint by phone. Ask the agent to log it as a formal complaint.

## What happens next

We confirm we've received it within 1 business day and give you a reference number. You'll get our final response within:

| Country | Final response within |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 10 business days |
| UAE | 15 business days |
| Egypt | 15 business days |

## If you're not satisfied

If you disagree with our final response, or haven't had one in time, you can take your complaint to the central bank's consumer protection department in your country. Our final response explains how.

A complaint doesn't replace a dispute. If you want money back for a transaction, open a dispute first, within the deadline; a complaint about the same transaction doesn't stop the dispute deadline from running.

title: How long we keep your data
headings: Can I ask you to delete my data?
text:
How long we keep your data
Section: Legal > Privacy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We keep your data while your account is open, and for a period after it's closed, because the law requires payment companies to keep records.

## After you close your account

| Country | We keep your records for |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 10 years after closure |
| UAE | 5 years after closure |
| Egypt | 5 years after closure |

This includes your identity documents, transactions and our messages with you. After that, the data is deleted or anonymized.

## Can I ask you to delete my data?

You can ask, and we'll delete what we're allowed to, such as marketing preferences and device data. Records we have to keep by law can't be deleted before the end of the period above.

## Selfies and ID photos

Used for verification and fraud prevention, and kept for the same period as your other records.

If your account was part of a fraud investigation or legal case, we may have to keep the related records for longer, until the case is closed.

text:
Changes to our terms
Section: Legal > Terms
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We update our terms of use and privacy notice from time to time, for example when we add new features or when the law changes.

## How will I know?

We'll tell you at least 30 calendar days before a change takes effect, by email and in the app. The message summarizes what's changing, and the new version is available in **Profile** > **Legal**.

## Do I have to accept?

If you keep using your account after the change takes effect, you're treated as having accepted it. If you don't agree, you can close your account for free before that date. See Closing your account.

Previous versions of our terms are listed in **Profile** > **Legal** > **Previous versions**, with the dates they applied.

Changes that are only in your favour, such as a new free service, and changes required immediately by law or a regulator, can apply without notice.

title: Accounts of deceased customers
headings: What about payments after the date of death?
text:
Accounts of deceased customers
Section: Legal > Account status
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We're sorry for your loss. This explains how a family member or legal representative can tell us about a death and receive the account balance.

## Tell us

Contact us through our website's contact form or by phone. You don't need a Sahla Pay account yourself. We'll freeze the account straight away, so no payments can be made from it.

## Documents we'll need

- The death certificate
- Your own ID
- A document showing you're entitled to the balance, such as an inheritance deed (a court-issued heirs certificate) or a court order

## How the balance is paid

Once we've checked the documents, we pay the balance to the heirs, to a bank account in their names, as set out in the inheritance document. If there are several heirs, we pay each one their share, or a single representative appointed by all of them.

## What about payments after the date of death?

Card payments and transfers made after the date of death are reviewed. Scheduled transfers and subscriptions are cancelled.

We can't share account details, transactions or statements with anyone until we've received the inheritance documents, even with close family members.

title: Restricted countries and transactions
text:
Restricted countries and transactions
Section: Legal > Restrictions
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some payments aren't allowed with Sahla Pay, because of international sanctions, local laws or a high risk of fraud.

## Restricted countries

We can't process international transfers to, or card payments in, countries under comprehensive international sanctions. The list changes, so we don't publish it here. If you try to make a payment to a restricted country, the app tells you before you confirm.

## Restricted transactions

You can't use Sahla Pay for:

- gambling and betting, where it's illegal in your country
- buying or selling cryptocurrency
- adult content
- weapons, drugs or other illegal goods
- paying for or receiving money on behalf of someone else, as a business

Card payments to these merchants are declined, and transfers that look like these activities may be held for review.

## What if I didn't know?

If a payment is blocked, nothing is taken from your balance. If we find your account has been used for restricted activities, we may restrict or close it.

Connecting through a VPN that shows a location in a restricted country also blocks your transactions, even if you're not there. See Using Sahla Pay with a VPN.

If you confirm it after the cut-off time on a business day, or on a day that is not a business day, it is treated as received on the next business day, except for transfers between Sahla Pay users, QR payments and card payments, which we process at any time.

This Privacy Notice explains how Sahla Pay collects, uses, shares and protects your personal data when you use our app and services. ## 1. Who is responsible for your data

The Sahla Pay company that provides your account in your country is responsible for your personal data, as the data controller under the personal data protection law of that country. If you have an account in one country and send money to someone in another, each company is responsible for the data it holds.

### 2.1 Data you give us

- **Financial and background data:** your occupation, the purpose of your account, the source of your funds, and documents you provide to support these, such as payslips or contracts.
- **Communications:** messages, chats, call recordings, complaints and feedback.

- **Your representatives:** for example, a guardian approving a minor's account in Egypt, or heirs after a customer's death, once they have proved their entitlement.

Section: Legal > Privacy Notice
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## 6. International transfers of data

Some of our service providers process data outside your country. Where the law of your country restricts transfers abroad, we transfer data only where it is permitted, for example with the approval of the competent authority or with appropriate contractual safeguards. Data about accounts in Saudi Arabia that the law requires to remain in the Kingdom is stored there.

## 7. How long we keep your data

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Privacy Notice
Section: Legal > Privacy Notice
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## 8. Your rights

Depending on the law of your country, you have the right to:

- be informed about how we use your data, as in this notice;
- access a copy of your data;
- correct data that is wrong or incomplete;
- ask us to delete your data, where we are not required to keep it;
- withdraw your consent, for example to marketing, at any time;
- object to some uses of your data, and ask for a person to review an automated decision.

To use your rights, contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us** or **Profile** > **Privacy**. We will confirm your identity first. We will answer within the time allowed by the law of your country.

Some requests can't be met in full. We can't delete identity documents, transaction records or verification data before the end of the retention period, because the law requires us to keep them, and we can't give you data about another person, such as the full details of someone who sent you money.

## 9. Security

We protect your data with encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls, monitoring and regular security testing. Our staff can access your data only when their role requires it, and every access is logged. Support staff can see the last four digits of your card, never the full number, PIN or security code.

## 10. Marketing

We send you marketing messages only if you have agreed to them. You can turn them off at any time in **Profile** > **Notifications**. Service messages, security alerts and notices we are legally required to send are not marketing, and can't be turned off.

Section: Legal > Fees and Charges Schedule
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## 5. Fees that are waived or refunded

- A card that stops working within 12 months of issue, without physical damage, is replaced free of charge.
- A card that never arrives is replaced free of charge, unless the courier's records show it was delivered and signed for.
- A card retained by an ATM is replaced without the lost card fee.
- Transfer fees are refunded if a transfer fails or is returned by the recipient's bank.
- The fee for recalling an international transfer is not refunded, even if the recall fails.
- Card top-up fees are not refunded if you later move the money out of your account.
- The dormancy fee is never charged if your balance is zero, and never reduces your balance below zero.

## 6. Changes to fees

We will give you at least 30 calendar days notice before increasing a fee or introducing a new fee. Reductions may apply immediately. Changes required by law, including changes to the rate of VAT, apply from the date set by law.

title: Dispute, Refund and Chargeback Policy
headings: 2. Refunds from merchants > 2.1 Who issues refunds
text:
Dispute, Refund and Chargeback Policy
Section: Legal > Dispute > Refund and Chargeback Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

This policy explains how Sahla Pay handles refunds, disputes about transfers and card payments, and chargebacks. It supplements clause 12 of the Terms of Use. Where this policy refers to days, it means calendar days unless it says business days.

## 1. Scope

This policy covers:

- refunds issued by merchants for card and QR payments;
- payments that failed but were deducted from your balance;
- transfers sent to the wrong recipient;
- card payments you dispute because of a problem with the merchant;
- ATM withdrawals where the cash was not dispensed.

Payments you did not authorize are handled under the Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy, which gives you stronger protection. If you are unsure which applies, report the problem from the transaction in the app and we will choose the right process.

### 2.1 Who issues refunds

Only the merchant can issue a refund for a card or QR payment. You should first ask the merchant. We cannot oblige a merchant to accept a return that its own policy does not allow, but if a merchant breaks its own policy or a written promise, you may dispute the payment.

### 2.2 Refund times

| Country | Card refund credited within, after the merchant issues it |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 7 business days |
| UAE | 10 business days |
| Egypt | 14 business days |

QR refunds are credited immediately when the merchant sends them. Refunds are credited to your balance, including when the card used for the payment has expired, been replaced or been closed.

This policy explains how Sahla Pay handles refunds, disputes about transfers and card payments, and chargebacks. It supplements clause 12 of the Terms of Use. Where this policy refers to days, it means calendar days unless it says business days.

## 1. Scope

This policy covers:

- refunds issued by merchants for card and QR payments;
- payments that failed but were deducted from your balance;
- transfers sent to the wrong recipient;
- card payments you dispute because of a problem with the merchant;
- ATM withdrawals where the cash was not dispensed.

Payments you did not authorize are handled under the Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy, which gives you stronger protection. If you are unsure which applies, report the problem from the transaction in the app and we will choose the right process.

### 2.1 Who issues refunds

Only the merchant can issue a refund for a card or QR payment. You should first ask the merchant. We cannot oblige a merchant to accept a return that its own policy does not allow, but if a merchant breaks its own policy or a written promise, you may dispute the payment.

### 2.2 Refund times

| Country | Card refund credited within, after the merchant issues it |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 7 business days |
| UAE | 10 business days |
| Egypt | 14 business days |

QR refunds are credited immediately when the merchant sends them. Refunds are credited to your balance, including when the card used for the payment has expired, been replaced or been closed.

If the dispute is approved, the recoverable amount is returned to your balance within 5 business days in Saudi Arabia, 7 business days in the UAE and 10 business days in Egypt after the decision. We can only recover money still held by the recipient. Where part of the money has already been spent or withdrawn, we return what we can recover and close the case. No temporary credit is given for wrong-transfer disputes.

### 4.4 International transfers

International transfers can only be recalled through the receiving bank, which decides whether to return the money. A recall fee applies, as set out in the Fees and Charges Schedule, and is not refunded if the recall fails.

### 5.1 Reasons for a dispute

You may dispute a card payment if you were charged more than once or charged the wrong amount, if goods or services were not provided, if goods were significantly not as described, or if a merchant did not process a refund it agreed to. You should contact the merchant before opening a dispute and keep a record of your contact.

### 5.2 Deadlines

The dispute must be opened within the period in clause 4.2, counted from the transaction date. For goods or services due to be delivered at a later date, the period is counted from the expected delivery date, but a dispute for non-delivery may only be opened 15 calendar days after that date.

### 5.3 Temporary credit

If a card dispute is still open 10 business days after you submitted it, we usually credit the amount to your balance temporarily. If the dispute is decided in the merchant's favour or you cancel it, we will deduct the temporary credit.

### 5.4 Chargebacks

Where a card dispute qualifies under the card network's rules, we raise a chargeback with the merchant's bank. The merchant may accept it or provide evidence in response. The complete process can take up to 90 calendar days. Chargebacks are not available for QR payments, for transfers, or for payments to gambling or cryptocurrency merchants; disputes involving those merchants are reviewed only as possible fraud.

title: Customer Identification and Anti-Money Laundering Policy
text:
Customer Identification and Anti-Money Laundering Policy
Section: Legal > Customer Identification and AML Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sahla Pay is required by law to know who our customers are, to understand how their accounts are used, and to report suspicious activity to the authorities. This policy explains, for customers, what that means in practice.

## 1. Why we do this

Anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing laws in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt apply to all payment and e-money providers. They require us to identify customers, monitor transactions and keep records. These requirements protect the financial system, and they also protect you, by making it harder for criminals to open accounts in your name or use your account.

### 2.1 Documents

To verify an account we require:

| Country | Identity document | Proof of address |
|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | a valid Saudi national ID or Iqama | not required |
| UAE | a valid Emirates ID | only in some cases, dated within 3 months |
| Egypt | a valid Egyptian national ID card | required, dated within 3 months |

We also require a live selfie to confirm that the document belongs to the person opening the account. Digital identity services, Nafath in Saudi Arabia and UAE Pass in the UAE, may be used instead of scanning a document, but the selfie is still required.

### 2.2 Review times

Most verifications are completed automatically. Where a manual review is needed, it takes up to 1 business day in Saudi Arabia, 2 business days in the UAE and 3 business days in Egypt.

### 2.3 Accounts we cannot open

We do not open accounts for people who appear on sanctions lists, for people who are not resident in the country where they apply, for anyone acting on behalf of another person or a business, or where we cannot verify the information provided.

### 3.1 Questions at account opening

When you open an account, we ask about your occupation and the main purpose of the account. Your answers help us recognize activity that is normal for you.

### 3.2 Source of funds

When your account receives large amounts, or the pattern of your activity changes, we may ask where the money comes from. We normally ask when the money you receive in a calendar month exceeds SAR 50,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 50,000 in the UAE or EGP 250,000 in Egypt, but we may ask at any amount. Typical evidence includes a salary certificate, a contract of sale or a bank statement.

### 3.3 Periodic review

We review customer information regularly and ask customers to re-verify at least every 2 years, and whenever their identity document expires.

headings: 5. What happens if you don't provide information
text:
Customer Identification and Anti-Money Laundering Policy
Section: Legal > Customer Identification and AML Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## 4. Monitoring transactions

We monitor transactions automatically and, where needed, manually. We may hold a payment for review before processing it, ask you questions about it, or decline it. Common reasons include payments to many new recipients in a short time, payments that don't match the purpose you gave us, and payments connected to countries subject to sanctions.

Transfers held for review are usually reviewed within a few hours. The execution times in the Terms of Use start only after the review is complete.

## 5. What happens if you don't provide information

If you don't provide information we request by the date in our message, we will restrict outgoing payments from your account until you do. If you still don't provide it, or if the information doesn't satisfy our legal obligations, we may close your account with notice, and pay your balance to a bank account in your name.

## 6. Reporting to the authorities

Where we suspect money laundering, terrorist financing or another crime, the law requires us to report it to the financial intelligence unit in your country. The law also prohibits us from telling you that we have made a report, or that an investigation is taking place. In these situations, we may restrict your account without explaining why, and we may not be able to tell you when the restriction will end.

## 7. Record keeping

We keep identification documents, transaction records and records of our checks for 10 years after the account closes in Saudi Arabia, and 5 years in the UAE and 5 years in Egypt, or longer if an investigation requires it.

title: Complaints Handling Policy
text:
Complaints Handling Policy
Section: Legal > Complaints Handling Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

We want to know when we get things wrong. This policy explains how to make a complaint, how we handle it, and what you can do if you're not satisfied with our answer.

## 1. What counts as a complaint

A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction about our products, services, staff or decisions, where you expect a response. You don't need to use the word "complaint". If you raise a problem with our support team and say you're unhappy with how it was handled, we will treat it as a complaint.

A complaint is different from a request to dispute a transaction. If you want money back for a specific payment, you should open a dispute first, within the dispute deadline. Making a complaint does not stop the dispute deadline from running.

## 2. How to complain

You can complain:

- in the app, through **Help** > **Make a complaint**;
- by phone, by asking the agent to register a formal complaint;
- in writing, to the address shown in the app under **Profile** > **Legal**.

Complaints can be made in Arabic or English. Someone else may complain on your behalf, such as a family member or lawyer, if you give us your consent in the app or in writing.

## 3. What we need from you

Please tell us what happened, when, which transactions are involved, and what you would like us to do. Include any screenshots, receipts or messages that support your complaint.

### 4.1 Acknowledgement

We will acknowledge your complaint within 1 business day and give you a reference number.

Where we find that we got something wrong, we will put it right. Depending on the case, this may include correcting your account, refunding fees or charges, paying interest or compensation for losses you suffered as a result of our error, or apologizing and explaining what we will change.

We record and analyse complaints to find and fix the causes of recurring problems. Complaint records are kept for the same period as other account records.

Making a complaint will never affect how we treat you or your account. Complaints that are abusive or threatening towards our staff may be handled in writing only.

title: Payment Links Seller Terms
text:
Payment Links Seller Terms
Section: Legal > Payment Links Seller Terms
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

These terms apply when you create a payment link to receive money for something you sell. They add to the Terms of Use. If you don't agree to them, don't create payment links.

## 1. What payment links are for

Payment links let you receive occasional payments for goods or services you sell personally, such as second-hand items, home-made food or private lessons. Anyone with a debit card can pay a link, whether or not they use Sahla Pay. Payment links are not a merchant service. You must not use them as the main way of collecting payments for a registered business, a shop, or anyone other than yourself.

## 2. Creating a link

Each link has a fixed amount and description that you set. Links expire after 30 calendar days if they are not paid. The maximum amount per link is SAR 2,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 2,000 in the UAE and EGP 5,000 in Egypt. You must describe what you are selling accurately and not use links for anything prohibited by our Acceptable Use Policy.

## 3. Fees

When a link is paid, we deduct a seller fee from the payment before crediting your balance: 1% in Saudi Arabia, 1% in the UAE and 1.5% in Egypt. The buyer pays only the amount on the link. Seller fees are not refunded if the payment is later refunded or reversed.

## 4. Your obligations as a seller

You must deliver what you described, on time, and handle questions and complaints from buyers yourself. You are responsible for any taxes or permits that apply to what you sell. If a buyer asks for a refund, you can refund them from the payment in **Activity**.

## 5. Buyer disputes and reversals

Buyers pay by card, so they can dispute the payment with their bank under card network rules, for example if they say the item never arrived. If a buyer disputes a payment, we will deduct the disputed amount from your balance while the dispute is open, and ask you for evidence of delivery. If the dispute is decided in the buyer's favour, the amount is not returned to you. If your balance is not enough to cover a disputed amount, you must repay the difference, and we may restrict your account until you do.

## 6. Limits on use

The money you receive through payment links counts towards your balance limit and may trigger a source of funds review. If you receive a large number of link payments, or payments that look like business activity, we may ask about your activity, limit or stop your use of payment links, or ask you to stop using your personal account for those sales.

## 7. Fraud and prohibited sales

If we believe a link is being used to sell something that doesn't exist, or to collect money by deception, we will block the link, hold the funds received through it, and may close your account. Funds held for this reason are released only to the buyers, or as required by the authorities.

## 8. Ending your use of payment links

You can stop using payment links at any time. We may stop you from using them, with notice, or immediately in the situations described in section 7. Links that have already been paid remain subject to these terms, including buyer disputes, for as long as a dispute can be raised.

You can stop using payment links at any time. We may stop you from using them, with notice, or immediately in the situations described in section 7. Links that have already been paid remain subject to these terms, including buyer disputes, for as long as a dispute can be raised.

By opening a Sahla Pay account, you agree to receive information, notices and documents from us electronically, and to sign agreements electronically. This consent forms part of the Terms of Use.

## 1. What we send electronically

We send electronically:

- the Terms of Use, Card Terms and Conditions, Fees and Charges Schedule, Privacy Notice and other policies, and any changes to them;
- statements, receipts and tax invoices;
- notices about your account, such as restrictions, dormancy and closure;
- security alerts and one-time passwords;
- responses to your disputes and complaints.

## 2. How we send it

We use one or more of these channels:

- the **Inbox** in the app;
- push notifications;
- SMS to your registered phone number;
- email to your verified email address.

A notice is treated as received when it is available in your app Inbox, or when we send it to your phone number or email address, whichever comes first. One-time passwords are sent by SMS only.

## 3. Electronic signatures

When you confirm an action in the app, for example by accepting terms, approving a payment with your passcode or biometrics, or entering a one-time password, that confirmation has the same effect as your signature on paper.

## 4. Keeping your details up to date

You must keep your phone number and email address up to date, so that you receive our communications. If we can't reach you because your details are out of date, notices sent to the details we hold are still treated as received.

## 5. Paper copies

You can download and save any document from the app. If you need a paper copy of a legal document, ask us through **Help** > **Chat with us**, and we'll send it free of charge.

title: Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy
text:
Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy
Section: Legal > Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

This policy explains what happens when a payment is made from your account without your permission, who bears the loss, and what you must do. It supplements clause 11 of the Terms of Use.

## 1. What is an unauthorized transaction

A transaction is unauthorized if it was made from your account or with your card without your consent, for example by someone who stole your card or phone, obtained your card details, or took over your account.

A transaction is **authorized**, even if you were deceived, if you approved it yourself: by confirming it in the app, entering your PIN, approving it with biometrics, or entering or sharing a one-time password. Payments made because of a scam, such as a fake seller or a fraudster pretending to be from a bank, are usually authorized transactions. They are covered by our fraud reporting process, not by this policy.

## 2. What you must do

As soon as you notice a transaction you didn't authorize, you must:

1. freeze your card in the app;
2. change your password;
3. report the transaction from **Activity**, or call our fraud line, which is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

## 3. Refunds of unauthorized transactions

If you report an unauthorized transaction within 2 calendar days of becoming aware of it, we will refund it in full once we have confirmed it was unauthorized, together with any fees charged on it.

We may investigate before refunding. If we have reasonable grounds to suspect fraud on your part, we may delay the refund and report the matter to the authorities.

headings: 4. Your liability > 4.2 Fraud and gross negligence
text:
Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy
Section: Legal > Unauthorized Transactions and Liability Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

### 4.1 Late reporting

If you report an unauthorized transaction later than the period in section 3, your liability for losses before you reported it is limited to:

| Country | Maximum liability |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | SAR 500 |
| UAE | AED 500 |
| Egypt | EGP 2,000 |

You have no liability for transactions made after you have reported your card or account as compromised.

### 4.2 Fraud and gross negligence

You are liable for all losses if you acted fraudulently, or if you intentionally or with gross negligence failed to keep your security details safe. Examples of gross negligence include sharing a one-time password with anyone, writing your PIN on your card, keeping your password with your phone, or giving another person access to your app.

### 4.3 Very late reporting

We can't refund unauthorized transactions that you report more than 13 months after the transaction date, except where the law of your country provides otherwise.

## 5. Our investigation

We will investigate every report. We may ask you for information, for example about how your card or details could have been obtained, and we may ask you to report the matter to the police. If our investigation shows that a transaction we refunded was in fact authorized by you, we may deduct the refund from your balance and will tell you why.

## 6. Account security after a report

After a report, we may block the affected card, log out all devices, and ask you to verify your identity again before you can use your account. We may also apply the security holds described in the Terms of Use, such as the block on new recipients after a change of device.

title: Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
section_path: Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
text:
Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
Section: Legal > Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

This policy explains when an account becomes dormant, what happens to it, and how money in inactive or closed accounts is protected.

## 1. When an account becomes dormant

An account becomes dormant if the customer doesn't initiate any transaction for the following period:

| Country | Period without customer activity |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 12 months |
| UAE | 12 months |
| Egypt | 18 months |

Customer activity means a transaction you make yourself, such as a top-up, transfer, card payment or bill payment. Money you receive, refunds and fees we charge are not customer activity. Logging in to the app without making a transaction is not activity either.

## 2. Before an account becomes dormant

We will send you at least two reminders, by email and in the app, before your account becomes dormant, explaining how to keep it active.

## 3. Effects of dormancy

While an account is dormant:

- your card is suspended and is not renewed when it expires;
- you can still log in, view your balance and receive money;
- a monthly dormancy fee applies: no fee in Saudi Arabia, AED 10 per month in the UAE and EGP 20 per month in Egypt.

The dormancy fee is only taken from your balance. It is never charged when your balance is zero, and it never reduces your balance below zero. No debt is created.

## 4. Reactivating an account

You can reactivate a dormant account by making any transaction yourself. If your identity document has expired, you'll need to upload a valid one first. Dormancy fees stop from the following month. Fees already charged are not refunded.

text:
Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
Section: Legal > Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Funds Policy
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## 5. Closure of dormant accounts

If a dormant account has a zero balance for a further 12 months, we may close it, after notifying you. A dormant account with money in it is not closed only because it is dormant.

## 6. Unclaimed funds

Money in a dormant account remains yours. Where the law of your country requires, after a long period without contact we may transfer the balance to the authority responsible for unclaimed funds, after trying to contact you through all the details we hold. You or your heirs can claim the money from us, or from that authority, at any time.

## 7. Refunds and payments after closure

If money is received for an account that has been closed, we forward it to the bank account nominated at closure. If that is not possible, for example because the bank account has also been closed, we hold the money as unclaimed funds under section 6.

## 8. Deceased customers

If we learn that a customer has died, the account is frozen and is not treated as dormant. The balance is paid to the heirs once they have provided the documents we require.

text:
Sending money to India
Section: Transfers > International > Destinations
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

You can send money from your Sahla Pay balance to a bank account in India, if your account is registered in Saudi Arabia or the UAE and is verified. The recipient receives Indian rupees (INR).

## What your recipient needs to give you

- the recipient's full name exactly as their bank has it
- their bank account number
- the bank's IFSC code, an 11-character code found on their cheque book or banking app

Ask the recipient to send you these details in writing, for example by copying them from their banking app, rather than reading them out. Most returned transfers are caused by a wrong digit or a name that doesn't match.

## How to send

To send money to India:

1. Tap **Send** > **International** and choose India.
2. Enter the amount, in your currency or in Indian rupees (INR).
3. Enter the recipient's details, or choose a saved recipient.
4. Check the exchange rate, the fee and the amount the recipient will get.
5. Tap **Confirm** and enter the one-time password we send you.

The exchange rate is fixed when you confirm.

title: Sending money to India
headings: Things to know about this destination
text:
Sending money to India
Section: Transfers > International > Destinations
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

## Things to know about this destination

Most Indian banks credit incoming transfers through the instant payment network, including on weekends and Indian public holidays. A few smaller cooperative banks only process them on their working days.

For larger amounts, the recipient's bank may ask them to confirm the purpose of the payment or to provide their PAN. This happens on their side and doesn't delay the money leaving Sahla Pay.

Transfers to Indian bank accounts are always paid out in rupees. You can't send dollars or riyals to an Indian account through Sahla Pay.

## If something goes wrong

If the receiving bank rejects the transfer, the full amount, including our fee, comes back to your balance in your own currency, at the exchange rate on the day it's returned. If you sent it to the wrong person, you can ask us to recall it, but a recall fee applies and the receiving bank decides whether to return the money. See Disputes for international transfers.

Pakistani banks require the recipient's CNIC for every incoming international transfer. If it's missing or doesn't match the account, the transfer is returned.

Transfers usually arrive within the hour, but on the last few days of Ramadan and before Eid, volumes are very high and some banks take longer.

Each transfer to Pakistan is limited by our payout partner, separately from your own daily limit. To send more, make another transfer; each one is charged separately.

## If something goes wrong

If the receiving bank rejects the transfer, the full amount, including our fee, comes back to your balance in your own currency, at the exchange rate on the day it's returned. If you sent it to the wrong person, you can ask us to recall it, but a recall fee applies and the receiving bank decides whether to return the money. See Disputes for international transfers.

3. Enter the recipient's details, or choose a saved recipient.
4. Check the exchange rate, the fee and the amount the recipient will get.
5. Tap **Confirm** and enter the one-time password we send you.

The exchange rate is fixed when you confirm.

3. Enter the recipient's details, or choose a saved recipient.
4. Check the exchange rate, the fee and the amount the recipient will get.
5. Tap **Confirm** and enter the one-time password we send you.

The exchange rate is fixed when you confirm.

text:
Sending money to Sudan
Section: Transfers > International > Destinations
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

Sending money to Sudan is not available from Saudi Arabia and not available from the UAE at the moment, because of the disruption to the banking system and the restrictions that apply to transfers into the country.

## Can I send money to someone from Sudan who lives elsewhere?

Yes. The restriction is about where the money is sent, not about the recipient's nationality. You can send to a bank account in any country where international transfers are available.

## Can I pay with my card in Sudan?

Card payments and ATM withdrawals in Sudan are also declined while the restriction applies.

## Will this change?

We review restricted destinations regularly. When transfers to Sudan become available again, the country will appear in the list under **Send** > **International**.

## I received money from Sudan

Incoming transfers from Sudan may be held for review or returned to the sender, depending on the sending bank and the route the money took. See Restricted countries and transactions.

title: Using your card in Türkiye
text:
Using your card in Türkiye
Section: Cards > Using your card abroad > Destinations
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your Sahla Pay card works in Türkiye wherever the card network logo is shown, for payments in shops, online and at ATMs. The local currency is Turkish lira.

## Before you travel

- Check that **International payments** is switched on in **Cards** > **Card settings**.
- Top up enough to cover your trip, plus some extra for hotel and car rental holds.
- Keep your phone number active while roaming, because we may send you a code to approve a payment.
- Note the fraud line number from **Help** > **Call us**. It's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

## Paying in local currency

When a card machine or ATM offers to charge you in your own currency instead of Turkish lira, choose Turkish lira. If you accept the conversion, the shop's or ATM's exchange rate is used, which is usually worse than ours.

headings: If your card is lost or stolen
text:
Using your card in Türkiye
Section: Cards > Using your card abroad > Destinations
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Local tips

Cards are accepted almost everywhere in cities, including taxis in Istanbul. Smaller shops in markets and villages may prefer cash.

Prices in tourist areas are sometimes shown in euros or dollars. Pay in lira; card machines that offer to charge you in your own currency use the shop's exchange rate, not ours.

Many ATMs in Türkiye add their own fee, shown on the screen before you confirm. Bank-branch ATMs usually charge less than standalone machines in tourist areas.

## If your card is lost or stolen

Freeze it straight away in **Cards** > **Freeze**. If you can't find it, report it as lost in the app. We can only deliver replacement cards to an address in the country your account is registered in, so use your virtual card or a mobile wallet for the rest of your trip.

title: Hajj and Umrah: paying and spending
text:
Hajj and Umrah: paying and spending
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Whether you're performing Hajj or Umrah from inside Saudi Arabia or travelling from the UAE or Egypt, here's how to use Sahla Pay for the journey, from paying your package to spending in Makkah and Madinah.

## Paying for your package

Licensed Hajj and Umrah companies accept payment in different ways. Ask your company which ones they accept before you book.

- **By card:** pay online or at the company's office with your Sahla Pay card. Card payments are limited to SAR 20,000 a day in Saudi Arabia, AED 20,000 in the UAE and EGP 50,000 in Egypt.
- **By bank transfer:** send money to the company's bank account from **Send** > **To a bank account**, in your own country. Keep the receipt from **Activity** as proof of payment.
- **By SADAD:** some packages booked in Saudi Arabia are paid by SADAD bill. See Paying government bills with SADAD.

Only pay companies licensed by the authorities. Fake Hajj and Umrah offers on social media are a common scam, especially before the season. See Investment scams and fake sellers.

## Spending in Makkah and Madinah

Cards and contactless are accepted in hotels, restaurants, supermarkets and most shops around the Haramain. Some street sellers and small stalls take cash only, so carry a little. ATMs near the mosques are very busy during the season; withdraw what you need before the peak days.

## Keeping your money safe during the season

Crowds make phones and wallets easy targets. Keep only the card you need with you, use your phone's lock screen, and know how to freeze your card in the app. If something is stolen, call our fraud line, which is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

During Hajj, the days of Arafah and Eid al-Adha are public holidays in all three countries. Bank transfers in the UAE and international transfers are processed on the next business day, so pay any remaining balance to your Hajj company well before the season starts. Transfers between Sahla Pay users and card payments are not affected.

title: Ramadan and Eid: sending Eidiya and managing busy days
text:
Ramadan and Eid: sending Eidiya and managing busy days
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Ramadan and Eid are the busiest weeks of the year for transfers. Here's how to send Eidiya, plan around the holidays, and avoid the most common problems.

## Sending Eidiya

The quickest way to send Eidiya to family and friends who use Sahla Pay is a normal transfer to their phone number. It's free and arrives instantly, even on the day of Eid.

To send to several people at once:

1. Tap **Send** > **To a Sahla Pay user**.
2. Tap **Add more people** and choose the contacts you want to send to.
3. Enter the amount for each person. You can send everyone the same amount, or different amounts.
4. Add a note, for example "Eid Mubarak", and tap **Send**.

If someone doesn't have Sahla Pay yet, they'll get an SMS to join. If they don't claim the money within 14 calendar days, it comes back to you.

## Sending Eidiya abroad

From Saudi Arabia and the UAE, you can send money to family abroad by international transfer. Banks in many countries are closed for several days over Eid, so send it a few days early if you want it to arrive in time. See the guide for your destination under **Transfers** > **International** > **Destinations**, for example Sending money to Pakistan.
