title: Ramadan and Eid: sending Eidiya and managing busy days
text:
Ramadan and Eid: sending Eidiya and managing busy days
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Holidays and transfer times

Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are public holidays in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt, and the exact dates depend on the moon. During the holidays:

- transfers between Sahla Pay users, QR payments and card payments work as normal;
- local bank transfers still arrive within a few minutes (including weekends) in Saudi Arabia and within a few minutes (including weekends) in Egypt;
- local bank transfers in the UAE, and international transfers, wait for the next business day;
- bill payments are posted to the company after the holiday.

## Support during Ramadan

Chat and phone support are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in Saudi Arabia and 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in the UAE, as usual. In Egypt, support hours may change during Ramadan; we announce any changes in the app. The fraud line is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in all three countries, whatever the date.

## Watch out for Eid scams

Fraudsters send fake "Eid gift" and "Ramadan prize" messages with links. We never send prizes that ask you to log in or enter a code. See Recognizing phishing and scam messages.

Scheduled transfers that fall on Eid are sent as usual at 8:00 AM local time, but if they go to a bank account in the UAE, the receiving bank only credits them after the holiday. Monthly rent or family transfers scheduled for the first of the month may arrive several days late if the first falls on Eid.

title: Paying rent with Sahla Pay
text:

Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can pay rent from your Sahla Pay balance by bank transfer to your landlord, and set it up to repeat every month. Here's what to know in each country.

## Paying your landlord

To pay rent by bank transfer:

1. Ask your landlord or agent for the IBAN and the name on their bank account.
2. Tap **Send** > **To a bank account** and enter the details.
3. In the reference, write the property and the month, for example "Flat 12, March rent".
4. Tap **Send later** and choose **Monthly**, if you want it to repeat. See Scheduled and recurring transfers.

Keep the receipts from **Activity**. They're your proof of payment if there's ever a disagreement.

title: Paying school and university fees
headings: Paying a school or university in your country
text:
Paying school and university fees
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

School and university fees are often one of the largest payments of the year. Here's how to pay them with Sahla Pay.

## Paying a school or university in your country

Schools usually accept one or more of these:

- **Card payment** through the school's online portal. Card payments are limited to SAR 20,000 a day in Saudi Arabia, AED 20,000 in the UAE and EGP 50,000 in Egypt.
- **Bank transfer** to the school's account. Use the student's name and ID number as the reference, so the school can match the payment.
- **Bill payment**, where the school is listed under **Payments** > **Bills** > **Education**.

Ask the school which method it prefers and how long it takes to confirm a payment. Pay at least a few days before the deadline.

## Paying in instalments

Many schools let you pay in terms. Set up a scheduled transfer for each instalment date, so you don't miss one. See Scheduled and recurring transfers.

title: Receiving your salary in Sahla Pay
headings: Will my salary count towards my limits?
text:
Receiving your salary in Sahla Pay
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can have your salary paid straight into your Sahla Pay balance, as long as your employer pays by bank transfer.

## What to give your employer

Your Sahla Pay IBAN and the name on your account. You'll find both in **Add money** > **Bank transfer**. Tap **Share** to send them as a PDF, which many HR departments ask for. You can also download an account confirmation letter from **Profile** > **Statements** > **Account letter**.

## When will it arrive?

Salary payments arrive like any bank transfer: within a few minutes in Saudi Arabia, 1 business day in the UAE and within a few minutes in Egypt, after your employer's bank sends it.

## Will my salary count towards my limits?

Receiving money doesn't count towards your sending limits. It does count towards your balance limit, which is SAR 100,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 75,000 in the UAE and EGP 300,000 in Egypt for verified accounts. If a salary payment would take you over it, it's returned to your employer, so move money out regularly if your balance is high.

Your account must be verified to receive a salary. Unverified accounts can only receive SAR 10,000 a month in Saudi Arabia, AED 7,500 in the UAE and EGP 40,000 in Egypt, which a salary usually exceeds.

## Salaries paid through the UAE Wage Protection System

In the UAE, many employers pay salaries through the Wage Protection System (WPS), which only pays into accounts with banks and exchange houses registered as WPS agents. title: New to Saudi Arabia or the UAE: getting started
headings: Before your residency ID is issued
Once you have your residency ID
text:
New to Saudi Arabia or the UAE: getting started
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

Just moved for work? Here's how to get set up with Sahla Pay, from your first days to sending money home.

## What you need

- A local mobile number in your own name.
- Your residency ID once it's issued: a valid Saudi national ID or Iqama in Saudi Arabia, or a valid Emirates ID in the UAE.
- Your employer's details, if you plan to receive your salary into Sahla Pay.

## Before your residency ID is issued

You can open an account and use it at the unverified level, but you can't verify with your passport or entry visa. Until you verify, you can hold up to SAR 5,000 in Saudi Arabia or AED 3,000 in the UAE, send up to SAR 1,000 or AED 1,000 a day to other Sahla Pay users, and you can't send money abroad or get a card.

## Once you have your residency ID

Verify in **Profile** > **Verify identity**. In Saudi Arabia, the fastest way is Nafath; in the UAE, UAE Pass. See Verifying with Nafath and Verifying with UAE Pass. After you're verified, you can get a card and start sending money home.

## Sending money home

International transfers are available as soon as you're verified. Check the guide for your home country, for example Sending money to India or Sending money to the Philippines, for the details your family's bank needs and how long it takes.

title: Sending money home every month
headings: Can I schedule a monthly international transfer?
text:
Sending money home every month
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

Many customers send part of their salary to family abroad every month. Here's how to make it quick, cheaper and reliable.

## Save your recipients

The first time you send to a family member, save them as a recipient. Later transfers are just a few taps, and you won't need a one-time password again for the same recipient. See Saved recipients.

## Can I schedule a monthly international transfer?

Not at the moment. Scheduled and recurring transfers only work for transfers to Sahla Pay users and local bank accounts. For international transfers, set a monthly reminder in your phone instead, and send it manually.

## Keeping costs down

- **Send one larger transfer instead of several small ones.** Each transfer has a minimum fee of SAR 15 in Saudi Arabia or AED 15 in the UAE, so small transfers cost more per riyal or dirham.
- **Top up by bank transfer, not by card.** Card top-ups cost 1% in Saudi Arabia and 1.5% in the UAE, plus VAT. Bank transfers are free.
- **Compare the amount the recipient gets.** The app shows the exchange rate and the final amount before you confirm.

## Timing

Most transfers arrive within hours, but banks in many countries are closed at weekends and on holidays, and these differ from Saudi Arabia's and the UAE's. Check the guide for your destination country, such as Sending money to Pakistan or Sending money to Bangladesh.

title: Buying a car: paying a large amount safely
headings: Paying more than your daily limit
text:
Buying a car: paying a large amount safely
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A car is one of the biggest payments most people make. Here's how to pay for one with Sahla Pay, and how to avoid the scams that target car buyers.

## Buying from a dealer

Dealers usually accept a bank transfer or a card payment for the deposit, and a bank transfer for the rest. Ask for an invoice with the dealer's company name and IBAN, and check that the account name on the transfer screen matches the company.

## Buying from a private seller

Never pay a private seller before you've seen the car, checked its documents and confirmed that the seller is the registered owner. Pay only when the ownership transfer is done or is being done in front of you. A transfer to a person can't be reversed if the car turns out not to exist; see Investment scams and fake sellers.

## Paying more than your daily limit

Your daily transfer limit is SAR 20,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 15,000 in the UAE and EGP 60,000 in Egypt.

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, you can ask for a temporary increase, up to SAR 50,000 in Saudi Arabia and AED 40,000 in the UAE, for 7 calendar days. Upload the car's sale agreement or the dealer's invoice. We review requests within 1 business day. See Requesting a temporary limit increase.

In Egypt, temporary increases are not available. Split the payment over several days, or pay the rest from a bank account.

## Your balance limit

To pay a large amount, you first need it in your balance, and your balance can't go above SAR 100,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 75,000 in the UAE or EGP 300,000 in Egypt. For a car that costs more than that, pay part from your bank directly.

title: Planning a wedding: managing big expenses
text:
Planning a wedding: managing big expenses
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Weddings involve many payments to many people: halls, caterers, photographers, dresses and gifts. Sahla Pay can help you keep track of them.

## Set money aside in Pockets

Create a **Wedding** pocket and move money into it each month. Money in a pocket isn't spent by card payments or transfers until you move it back, so it's protected from everyday spending. You can create up to 10 pockets, for example one for the hall and one for the honeymoon. See Budgeting with Pockets.

## Paying suppliers

- **Deposits:** pay by card where you can. If a supplier closes or doesn't deliver, card payments can be disputed; see Goods or services not received.
- **Bank transfers:** ask each supplier for an invoice with their company name and IBAN.
- **Sharing costs with family:** use payment requests, so everyone can pay their share with one tap; see Requesting money from friends.

## Large payments and limits

A hall or catering bill can be more than your daily limit. In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, you can request a temporary increase with the supplier's invoice; see Requesting a temporary limit increase. In Egypt, plan to pay large suppliers over several days.

## Wedding gifts

Gifts sent to you through Sahla Pay arrive instantly. If you receive a lot of money at once, it counts towards your balance limit, and very large amounts may lead to a source of funds question, which you can answer with a short explanation.

## Honeymoon abroad

Check the travel guide for your destination, and take your card details and the fraud line number with you. See Summer travel checklist.

title: Summer travel checklist
text:
Summer travel checklist
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Going away for the summer? Run through this list a week before you leave.

## A week before

1. **Check your card's expiry date** in **Cards** > **Show details**. If it expires while you're away, the renewal card is sent about 30 calendar days before expiry, to your home address. Activate it before you go.
2. **Check your ID's expiry date.** If it expires while you're away, payments are paused after the grace period.
3. **Turn on international payments** in **Card settings**.
4. **Add your card to a mobile wallet**, so you have a backup if your card is lost. Apple Pay is not available yet for accounts registered in Egypt; Google Pay works in all three countries.
5. **Read the guide for your destination**, for example Using your card in Türkiye or Using your card in the United Kingdom.

## Money

- Top up enough for your trip, and leave room for hotel and car rental holds, which can last up to 30 calendar days.
- Know your daily ATM limit: SAR 5,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 5,000 in the UAE or EGP 15,000 in Egypt.
- Always pay in the local currency, not your own.

## Security

- Keep your phone number active while roaming, because we may send you codes.
- Save the fraud line number from **Help** > **Call us**. It's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
- Avoid logging in through public Wi-Fi without a passcode lock on your phone, and turn off any VPN when using the app.

title: Helping a young family member in Egypt manage money
headings: What you can do as guardian
text:
Helping a young family member in Egypt manage money
Section: Guides > Life events
Countries: Egypt

In Egypt, young people can have their own Sahla Pay account from age 16. Until they're 21, a parent or legal guardian approves the account and can follow how it's used. Here's how it works from the guardian's side.

## Setting it up

1. Your son or daughter opens their own account and verifies it with their national ID.
2. In their app, they add you as guardian in **Profile** > **Guardian**.
3. You get a request in your own Sahla Pay app. Check the details and tap **Approve**.

You need a verified Sahla Pay account registered in Egypt to be a guardian.

## What you can do as guardian

- See their balance and transactions.
- Set a daily sending limit lower than the standard EGP 2,000.
- Freeze and unfreeze their card from your app.
- Send them pocket money, as a one-off or a scheduled weekly or monthly transfer.

## What you can't do

You can't send money out of their account, change their password, or read their chats with our support team.

## Pocket money ideas

Set up a scheduled monthly transfer on the 1st, and encourage them to create a pocket for something they're saving for. See Budgeting with Pockets.

## When they turn 21

Their account becomes a normal account automatically, and your guardian access ends. You don't need to do anything.

If you close your own Sahla Pay account, your child's account goes back to receive-only until another guardian approves it. Ask another parent or guardian to set it up before you close yours. See Accounts for minors and guardian consent.

3. You get a request in your own Sahla Pay app. Check the details and tap **Approve**.

You need a verified Sahla Pay account registered in Egypt to be a guardian.

## What you can do as guardian

- See their balance and transactions.
- Set a daily sending limit lower than the standard EGP 2,000.
- Freeze and unfreeze their card from your app.
- Send them pocket money, as a one-off or a scheduled weekly or monthly transfer.

## What you can't do

You can't send money out of their account, change their password, or read their chats with our support team.

## Pocket money ideas

Set up a scheduled monthly transfer on the 1st, and encourage them to create a pocket for something they're saving for. See Budgeting with Pockets.

## When they turn 21

Their account becomes a normal account automatically, and your guardian access ends. You don't need to do anything.

If you close your own Sahla Pay account, your child's account goes back to receive-only until another guardian approves it. Ask another parent or guardian to set it up before you close yours. See Accounts for minors and guardian consent.

title: Budgeting with Pockets
text:
Budgeting with Pockets
Section: Guides > Saving and budgeting
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Pockets let you set money aside inside your Sahla Pay account, for a goal or a regular bill, so you don't spend it by accident.

## How Pockets work

- You can have up to 10 pockets, each with its own name and, if you like, a target amount.
- Money in a pocket stays in your account, but card payments, QR payments and transfers only use your main balance.
- You can move money between your main balance and a pocket at any time, instantly and for free.

## Create a pocket

To create one:

1. On the home screen, tap **Pockets** > **New pocket**.
2. Give it a name, such as "Rent", "Emergency" or "Umrah".
3. Set a target amount, if you want one.
4. Move money in now, or set up an automatic weekly or monthly transfer from your main balance.

## Ideas

- **Bills pocket:** move your rent and bills into a pocket on salary day, so the money is there when they're due.
- **Emergency pocket:** build up a few months of expenses.
- **Goals:** travel, a wedding, a new phone, school fees.

## Pockets and your limits

Money in pockets counts towards your balance limit. Your home screen shows your main balance only; tap **Pockets** to see the total.

Pockets don't earn interest or profit, like the rest of your balance. If your account becomes dormant, the money in your pockets is treated like the rest of your balance, and dormancy fees can be taken from it when your main balance is empty.

title: Selling on the side: what Sahla Pay can and can't do
headings: What a personal account isn't for
text:
Selling on the side: what Sahla Pay can and can't do
Section: Guides > Getting paid
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you sell things occasionally, like home baking, handmade items, second-hand goods or private lessons, Sahla Pay can help you get paid. But a personal account isn't a business account, and there are limits to what it's for.

## Getting paid

- **From other Sahla Pay users:** ask them to send money to your phone number. It's free and instant.
- **From anyone with a debit card:** create a payment link and share it. See Payment links for small sellers.
- **By bank transfer:** share your Sahla Pay IBAN from **Add money** > **Bank transfer**.

## Payment link fees and limits

| Country | Seller fee | Maximum per link |
|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 1% | SAR 2,000 |
| UAE | 1% | AED 2,000 |
| Egypt | 1.5% | EGP 5,000 |

## What a personal account isn't for

You can't use Sahla Pay as the main account of a registered business, a shop, or a company. We don't offer business accounts; see Business accounts vs personal accounts. If your account starts to look like a business, with many payments from many different people, we may ask about your activity.

title: Selling on the side: what Sahla Pay can and can't do
text:
Selling on the side: what Sahla Pay can and can't do
Section: Guides > Getting paid > Keeping records
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Keeping records

Keep a simple list of what you sold, to whom and for how much. If we ask about the source of your funds, it's the quickest way to answer. Your statements in **Profile** > **Statements** show every payment.

Buyers who pay by payment link can dispute the payment with their bank. If they do, the amount is taken back from your balance while the dispute is open, even if you've already delivered. Keep proof of delivery, such as a photo or a signed note, for every sale.

title: Protecting older parents from scams
text:
Protecting older parents from scams
Section: Guides > Staying safe
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Older people are a common target for phone and message scams. If your parents use Sahla Pay, a few simple steps can protect their money.

## Talk about the golden rule

Nobody from Sahla Pay, a bank, the police or any government office will ever ask for a one-time password, PIN or password. If anyone asks, it's a scam, however official they sound. See We will never ask for your OTP.

## Set up the app together

- Turn on fingerprint or face login, so they don't need to type their password.
- Turn on **Code at every login** and **Passcode for transfers** in **Profile** > **Security**, for extra checks before money can move. See Two-step verification.
- Lower their daily card spending limit in **Card settings**, if they don't need the full amount.
- Turn on notifications, so they see every payment straight away.

## Scams to warn them about

- **"Your account is blocked"** calls and messages asking them to verify their details.
- **Family emergency** messages from a new number claiming to be a son or daughter who needs money urgently. Always call the family member on their usual number first.
- **Prize and refund** messages with a link.
- **Investment offers** with guaranteed returns.

## If something happens

Freeze the card in the app and call our fraud line, which is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can call together with your parent; we'll talk to you with their permission, but we'll need to confirm their identity with them directly. See Reporting fraud.

title: Protecting older parents from scams
section_path: Can I manage their account for them?
headings: Can I manage their account for them?
text:
Protecting older parents from scams
Section: Guides > Staying safe > Can I manage their account for them?
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Can I manage their account for them?

No. Each account belongs to one person, and only they can use it. You can't log in as them or approve payments on their behalf, even with their permission. If a parent can no longer manage their own money, ask us about the documents needed for a legal representative.
